**Surat al-Anfal**

Medinan, and it has seventy-five verses. It was said that seven verses, from His words ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾ to the end of seven verses, were revealed in Mecca. The more correct view is that it was revealed in Medina, even though the event it describes took place in Mecca.

* *

﴿They ask you about the spoils of war (al-anfal)﴾ and the rest of the verse. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: The reason for the revelation of this verse is that the Prophet ﷺ said on the day of Badr: "Whoever reaches such-and-such a place will have such-and-such a share of the nafl (extra spoils), whoever kills an enemy will have such-and-such, and whoever takes a captive will have such-and-such." When the two sides met, the young men hurried forward, while the elders and the notable men stayed by the banners. When God granted the Muslims victory, they came seeking what the Prophet ﷺ had promised them. The elders said: "We were a reserve for you. Had you been routed, you would have retreated to us. So do not take the spoils without us." Then Abu al-Yasar ibn Amr al-Ansari, of the Banu Salama, stood up and said: "O Messenger of God, you promised that whoever kills an enemy will have such-and-such, and whoever takes a captive will have such-and-such. We have killed seventy of them and taken seventy captive." Then Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said: "By God, O Messenger of God, what kept us from seeking what these men sought was not indifference to reward, nor cowardice before the enemy. Rather, we disliked leaving your flank exposed, lest cavalry of the polytheists attack from that side and strike you." The Messenger of God ﷺ then turned away from both of them. Sa'id said: "O Messenger of God, people are many and the spoils are small. If you give to those you mentioned, your companions will be left with very little." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war﴾.

[This reason for revelation is found in a number of reports which the author, may God have mercy on him, gathered together. They are in al-Tabari through several chains, with a sound isnad to Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. See: Tafsir al-Tabari 13/367-369; al-Mustadrak 2/326-327; al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi 6/315. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur 4/6; Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2/283-284.]

Ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of God ﷺ ordered that what was in the army's camp be gathered together, and the Muslims disagreed about it. Those who collected it said: "It belongs to us. The Messenger of God ﷺ had granted each man what he had captured." Those who had been fighting the enemy said: "Were it not for us, you would not have obtained it." Those who had been guarding the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "We had considered killing the enemy and taking the goods, but we feared for the Messenger of God ﷺ from the enemy's counterattack, and we stood between him and it. So you have no better claim to it than we do."

[Sirat Ibn Hisham 1/641-642 (Halabi edition).]

Makhul narrated from Abu Umama al-Bahili, who said: I asked 'Ubada ibn al-Samit about the anfal. He said: "It was revealed concerning us, the company of the people of Badr, when we disagreed about the nafl and our characters were corrupted by it. So God took it out of our hands and placed it under the authority of the Messenger of God ﷺ, who divided it among us equally (he said: 'on the basis of equality'). In that there was the fear of God, obedience to His Messenger, and the reconciling of hearts."

[See: al-Tabari 13/370-371; al-Mustadrak 2/326; al-Bayhaqi 6/292; Musnad of Imam Ahmad 5/322; Sirat Ibn Hisham 1/642. Al-Haythami, after attributing it to Imam Ahmad, said: "The men of both chains are trustworthy (thiqat)." See also the comment of Shaykh Mahmud Shakir on al-Tabari in the same place, and Ibn Kathir 2/284.]

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may God be pleased with him, said: On the day of Badr my brother 'Umayr was killed, and I killed Sa'id ibn al-'As ibn Umayya and took his sword, which was called Dhu al-Kathifa. It pleased me, so I brought it to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of God, God has healed my chest from the polytheists, so give me this sword." He said: "This is neither mine nor yours. Go and throw it into the qabad." So I threw it down and went back, with something in me that no one knows but God, because of the killing of my brother and the taking of my weapon. I said to myself: "Perhaps this sword will be given to one who has not shown the courage I have shown." I had not gone far when the messenger came to me, and God, mighty and majestic, had revealed: ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war﴾. I feared that something had been revealed concerning me. When I reached the Messenger of God ﷺ, he said: "O Sa'd, you asked me for the sword when it was not mine, but now it has become mine. So go and take it, for it is yours."

[Al-Tabari 13/373 through several chains. It was also related by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and Abu 'Ubayd in al-Amwal, and al-Hakim authenticated it (2/132), and al-Dhahabi agreed. See: Mahmud Shakir's comment on al-Tabari. Al-Qabad (with a fatha on the qaf and a fatha on the ba) is, in the sense of the verb, "what is gathered," namely the portion of the booty gathered before it is divided.]

'Ali ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The spoils belonged exclusively to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and no one else had any share in them. Whatever the Muslim expeditions (saraya) obtained, they brought to him. Whoever withheld from it even a needle or a thread was guilty of ghulul (embezzlement from the spoils).

[Al-Tabari 13/378, and al-Bayhaqi 6/293 in full. al-Suyuti also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh (al-Durr al-Manthur 4/8). Its chain is broken (munqati'), because 'Ali ibn Abi Talha did not hear the tafsir from Ibn 'Abbas.]

His words ﴿They ask you about the spoils of war﴾: that is, about the ruling on the anfal and its knowledge. This is a question seeking information, not a question seeking to obtain something. It was also said that it is a question seeking to obtain something; this was said by al-Dahhak and 'Ikrima. His words ﴿about the spoils of war﴾ mean "from the spoils of war," where 'an (about) has the sense of min (from). It was also said that 'an is a connecting particle, so that the meaning is "they ask you for the spoils," and this is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, which omits 'an. Al-anfal means the spoils (al-ghana'im). Its singular is nafl. Its root meaning is "increase." It is said: nafaltuka and anfaltuka, meaning "I gave you an increase." The spoils were called anfal because they are an increase from God, exalted is He, granted specially to this community.

Most of the exegetes hold that the verse concerns the spoils of Badr. 'Ata' said: The anfal are whatever came to the Muslims from the polytheists without fighting, such as a male or female slave or goods. Such things belong to the Prophet ﷺ, who does with them as he wishes.

His exalted words ﴿Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger﴾ [He divides them as He wills] (in the version "B": "they divide them as they both will"). The scholars differed about this. Mujahid, 'Ikrima, and al-Suddi said: This verse is abrogated (mansukha) by His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils, a fifth of it belongs to God and to the Messenger﴾, and so on. The spoils on that day belonged to the Prophet ﷺ, and God abrogated that ruling with the one-fifth share.

[See: Abu al-Qasim Hibat Allah ibn Salama, al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh, pp. 48-49. This is also reported from Mujahid and 'Ikrima. See al-Tabari 13/380-381.]

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: The verse is firmly established and not abrogated. The meaning of the verse is: ﴿Say: The spoils belong to God, together with this world and the Hereafter, and to the Messenger, who places them where God has commanded him.\u200f\u200f That is, the ruling concerning them belongs to God and His Messenger. God has explained their channels in His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain as spoils, a fifth of it belongs to God﴾, and so on.

[Reported by al-Tabari 13/381, who preferred that it is muhkam (not abrogated). He said: "The correct view on this is that God, mighty is His praise, informed that He made the anfal for His Prophet ﷺ, to grant them to whom he wills. He granted the slayer his spoils (salab), and assigned to the army in the initial raid (al-badi'a, the beginning of the military expedition) a quarter, and on the return a third after the fifth. He granted some people, beyond their shares, a camel each in some campaigns. So God, whose remembrance is great, placed the ruling on the anfal in the hands of His Prophet ﷺ, to give on the basis of what he sees as beneficial to the Muslims, and it is incumbent upon those after him among the leaders to follow his practice in this. There is nothing in the verse to show that its ruling is abrogated, since it admits of the meaning which I have described. It is not permissible to judge that a ruling revealed in the Qur'an is abrogated except by a proof which must be accepted. We have shown in more than one place in our books that there is no abrogation (naskh) except where a later ruling cancels the earlier ruling, eliminating it in all its meanings, or where a report comes which makes it binding that one of the two abrogates the other."]

﴿So fear God and set right your affairs among yourselves﴾: that is, fear God by obeying Him, and mend the state of affairs among you by abandoning dispute and opposition, and by committing the matter of the spoils to God and to His Messenger ﷺ.

﴿And obey God and His Messenger, if you are believers﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 8, verses 2–4:**

﴿Indeed, the believers are...﴾ He says: The believer is not the one who opposes Allah and His Messenger. Rather, "the believers" are those who are truthful in their faith. ﴿Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned﴾: their hearts become fearful and afraid. It is also said: when they are warned by Allah, they submit out of fear of His punishment.

﴿And when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾: in assent and certainty. ʿUmayr ibn Ḥabīb, who had been a companion (of the Prophet), said: "Faith has increase and decrease." It was asked: "What is its increase?" He said: "When we remember Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and praise Him, that is its increase; and when we forget and become heedless, that is its decrease." ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz wrote to ʿAdiyy ibn ʿAdiyy: "Faith has obligations (farāʾiḍ), conditions (sharāʾiṭ), laws (sharāʾiʿ), limits (ḥudūd) and sunan. Whoever completes them completes his faith, and whoever does not complete them has not completed his faith."

﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾: that is, they entrust their affairs to Him, trust in Him, hope for no one else, and fear no one other than Him.

﴿Those are the believers in truth﴾: meaning with certainty. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "They are free from disbelief." Muqatil said: "In truth, without doubt about their faith." In this there is evidence that it is not for everyone to describe himself as a believer in truth, because Allah only described with this specific people who have specific attributes, and not everyone truly possesses those attributes.

Ibn Abi Najih said: A man asked al-Ḥasan, "Are you a believer?" He replied: "If you are asking me about faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, Paradise and Hell, resurrection and reckoning, then I am a believer in them. But if you are asking me about His saying: 'The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned...' up to the end of the verse, then I do not know whether I am among them or not."

ʿAlqamah said: "We were on a journey and we met a people. We asked, 'Who are you?' They said, 'We are the believers in truth.' We did not know how to answer them until we met ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud and told him what they had said. He said, 'What did you reply to them?' We said, 'We did not reply to them with anything.' He said, 'Why did you not say: Are you among the people of Paradise? Indeed, the believers are the people of Paradise.'"

Sufyan al-Thawri said: "Whoever claims that he is a believer in truth, or in the sight of Allah, and does not testify that he is in Paradise, has believed in only half of the verse and not the other half."

﴿For them are degrees with their Lord﴾: ʿAṭāʾ said: "That means the degrees of Paradise, which they ascend through their deeds." Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: "They are seventy degrees, between each two degrees is the gallop of a well-trained horse for seventy years [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/390.]]" [144a].

﴿And forgiveness﴾ for their sins, ﴿and a noble provision﴾: good, meaning what He has prepared for them in Paradise.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 8, verses 5–7 (part 1 of 2):**

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth﴾. The scholars differed over what governs this *kaf* (the "as" in ﴿as your Lord brought you forth﴾). Al-Mubarrad said: its implied meaning is, "The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger, even though they dislike it, just as your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth, even though they disliked it." It was also said: its implied meaning is, "Proceed with the command of Allah concerning the spoils, even though they dislike it, just as you proceeded with the command of Allah to leave the house to pursue the caravan while they were averse."

ʿIkrimah said: its meaning is, "So fear Allah and set right your relations with one another, for that is better for you, just as the bringing forth of Muhammad (ﷺ) from his house in truth is better for you, even though a group among you disliked it."

Mujahid said: its meaning is, "As your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth despite the dislike of a group of them, so they dislike fighting and dispute about it."

It was also said: it refers back to His words, ﴿For them are degrees with their Lord﴾. Its implied meaning is: the promise of Allah of the degrees for them is a truth that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will fulfil, just as your Lord brought you forth from your house in truth, and He fulfilled the promise with victory and triumph.

It was also said: the *kaf* carries the meaning of *ʿala* ("upon"), and its implied meaning is: "Proceed upon that to which your Lord brought you forth."

Abu ʿUbaydah said: it is used figuratively in the sense of an oath, meaning "by the One who brought you forth," because *ma* is in the place of *alladhi* (who). Its response is ﴿they dispute with you﴾, and the oath falls upon it. Its implied meaning is: "They dispute with you, by Allah who brought you forth, your Lord, from your house in truth." It was also said: the *kaf* carries the meaning of *idh* ("when"), and its implied meaning is: "And remember when your Lord brought you forth."

It has been said: the intended "bringing forth" here is his departure from Makkah to Madinah. Most scholars, however, hold that what is meant is his departure from Madinah toward Badr, i.e., "just as your Lord commanded you to leave your house for Madinah in truth." It was said: "in truth" means "by revelation," in response to the pursuit of the polytheists, ﴿and indeed a group of the believers﴾ among them ﴿were averse﴾.

﴿They dispute with you concerning the truth﴾, i.e., concerning the fighting, ﴿after it has become clear﴾. This is because when the believers became certain of the fighting, they disliked it and said, "You did not inform us that we would meet the enemy so that we could prepare for their fighting; we only went out for the caravan." So that was their dispute after it had become clear to them that you do nothing except what you are commanded, and that your truthfulness in the promise was evident. ﴿As if they were being driven toward death﴾, due to the intensity of their aversion to fighting, ﴿while they were looking on﴾. There is an inversion in the wording; its implied sense is: "Indeed, a group of the believers are averse, as if they were being driven toward death while they were looking on, disputing with you concerning the truth after it had become clear."

Ibn Zayd said: these are the polytheists who disputed with him concerning the truth, as if they were being driven toward death when they were called to Islam, because of their aversion to it, while they were looking on.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and al-Suddi said: Abu Sufyan came from Syria with a caravan of the Quraysh, accompanied by forty riders from the disbelievers of Quraysh, among them ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs and Makhramah ibn Nawfal al-Zuhri. There was much wealth in it, and it was the *laṭīmah* [the caravan that carried perfume and merchandise]. When they came near Badr, news of this reached the Prophet (ﷺ), so he summoned his companions to it and informed them of the abundance of wealth and the small number of men with it. He said: "This is the caravan of Quraysh, in which are your possessions. Go out toward it; perhaps Allah will grant it to you as spoils." So the people responded to his call; some went out lightly, and some were reluctant. That was because they did not think that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would encounter war.

When Abu Sufyan heard of the Prophet's (ﷺ) march, he hired Damdam ibn ʿAmr al-Ghifari and sent him to Makkah, instructing him to go to Quraysh, call them to arms, and inform them that Muhammad had moved against their caravan with his companions. Damdam set out swiftly for Makkah.

Before Damdam's arrival in Makkah, by three nights, ʿAtikah bint ʿAbd al-Muttalib had seen a dream that frightened her. She sent to her brother al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib and said to him: "O my brother, by Allah, last night I saw a dream that frightened me, and I fear that some evil and calamity will befall your people because of it. So keep secret what I tell you." He said to her: "What did you see?" She said: "I saw a rider who came upon a camel until he stopped at al-Abtah, then he cried out at the top of his voice, 'Ho! Hasten, O people of Ghudur, to your slaughter within three days!' Then I saw people gather around him. Then he entered the mosque while the people followed him. While they were around him, his camel stumbled on the roof of the Kaʿbah, and he again cried out at the top of his voice with the same words, 'Ho! Hasten, O people of Ghudur, to your slaughter within three days!' Then his camel stumbled on the top of Abu Qubays, and he cried out with the same words. Then he took a rock and let it go, and it came falling until, when it reached the foot of the mountain, it shattered, and no house or dwelling in Makkah remained without a fragment of it entering it."

Al-ʿAbbas said: "By Allah, this is indeed a dream you have seen! Keep it secret, and do not mention it to anyone."

Then al-ʿAbbas went out and met al-Walid ibn ʿUtbah ibn Rabiʿah ibn ʿAbd Shams, who was his friend. He told him about it and asked him to keep it secret, but al-Walid mentioned it to his father ʿUtbah, and the matter spread until Quraysh was talking about it.

Al-ʿAbbas said: "I went out in the morning, circling the House, while Abu Jahl ibn Hisham was sitting with a group of Quraysh, discussing the dream of ʿAtikah. When Abu Jahl saw me, he said: 'O Abu al-Fadl, when you have finished your circumambulation, come to us.' He said: 'When I finished, I came and sat with them. Abu Jahl said to me: "O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, since when has this prophetess emerged among you?"'

I said: 'And what is that?'

He said: 'The dream that ʿAtikah saw.'

I said: 'And what did she see?'

He said: 'O sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, are you not content that your men prophesy, that now your women must prophesy too? ʿAtikah claims in her dream that he said, "Hasten within three days." So we will wait for these three days. If what she said is true, it will happen. If the three days pass and nothing of it occurs, we will write a document against you declaring that you are the most lying household among the Arabs.'"

Al-ʿAbbas said: "By Allah, I did nothing to him except deny it and reject that she had seen anything. Then we separated. When evening came, no woman of the sons of ʿAbd al-Muttalib remained but came to me and said: 'You have acquiesced to this wicked transgressor so that he insults your men, then he has even attacked the women, and you hear it! Yet there is no jealousy in you for anything you have heard?'

I said: 'By Allah, I have done much against him, and by Allah, if he returns, I will certainly deal with him for you.'"

He said: "On the third day after ʿAtikah's dream, I went out, eager and angry, thinking that some matter had escaped me from him that I wished to catch. I entered the mosque and saw him. By Allah, I was walking toward him, intending to confront him so that he would return to some of what he had said, and I would then strike him. He was a nimble man, sharp of face, sharp of tongue, and sharp of sight. Suddenly he came out running toward the gate of the mosque."

He said: "I said to myself: 'What is wrong with him, may Allah curse him? Is all this out of fear of me lest I insult him?' Then he had heard what I had not heard: the voice of Damdam ibn ʿAmr, who was shouting in the valley's bottom while standing on his camel. He had slit his camel's nose [that is, cut off its nose-ring or cut its nose], turned its saddle around, torn his shirt, and was saying: 'O assembly of Quraysh! The caravan, the caravan! Your wealth is with Abu Sufyan! Muhammad has moved against it with his companions! I do not think you will overtake it! Help! Help!'"

Then Iblis appeared to them in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Juʿshum, who was one of the nobles of Banu Bakr, and said: "I am a protector for you against Kinanah coming upon you from behind with anything you dislike."

So they set out quickly. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also went out with his companions, during nights that had passed in the month of Ramadan, until he reached a valley called Dhafiran. There news reached him of Quraysh's march to protect their caravan. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went on until, when he was at al-Rawha, he captured a spy of the people and was informed of them by him.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) also sent a spy of his own from Juhaynah, an ally of the Ansar, named ʿAbd Allah ibn Uraygit, who brought him news of the people. The caravan had outpaced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then Gabriel descended and said: "Indeed Allah has promised you one of the two groups: either the caravan or Quraysh." The caravan was dearer to them. So the Prophet (ﷺ) consulted his companions about pursuing the caravan or fighting the army.

Abu Bakr stood and spoke well. Then ʿUmar stood and spoke well. Then al-Miqdad ibn ʿAmr stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, proceed as Allah has shown you, for we are with you. By Allah, we will not say to you what the children of Israel said to Moses: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we will sit here.' Rather, we say: 'Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are fighting alongside you.' By He who sent you with truth, if you were to lead us to Bark al-Ghimad, meaning the city of Abyssinia, we would fight alongside you against whoever is in front of it until you reach it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said good things to him and prayed for good for him.

Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Advise me, O people," and he meant the Ansar, because they were the majority of the people. That was because when they pledged allegiance to him at al-ʿAqabah, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are free of your protection until you reach our homes. When you reach us, you are under our protection; we will defend you from what we defend our sons and women from." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) feared that the Ansar might think their support was owed only against an enemy who attacked him in Madinah, and that they were not obligated to march with him against an enemy outside their land.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that, Saʿd ibn Muʿadh said: "By Allah, it is as if you mean us, O Messenger of Allah?"

He said: "Yes."

He said: "We have believed in you, affirmed you, and testified that what you have brought is the truth. We have given you pledges and covenants of hearing and obedience upon that. So proceed, O Messenger of Allah, toward what you intend. By He who sent you with truth, if you were to lead us into this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge into it with you, and not one man of us would stay behind. We do not dislike that you bring us against your enemy tomorrow. Indeed, we are patient in war and truthful in encounter, and perhaps Allah will show you from us what will delight your eye. So march with us in the blessing of Allah."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was pleased with Saʿd's words, and this encouraged him. Then he said: "Proceed in the blessing of Allah and be glad, for Allah has promised me one of the two groups. By Allah, it is as though I am now looking at the places where the people will fall."

Thabit reported from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "This is the place where so-and-so will fall, and this is the place where so-and-so will fall." He said: and he would place his hand on the ground here and here. He said: No one moved from the place where the hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Allah promised you one of the two groups, that it would be yours﴾, meaning: one of the two groups, one of them being Abu Sufyan with the caravan, and the other being Abu Jahl with the war party.

﴿And you wished﴾, meaning: you desired, ﴿that the unarmed one would be yours﴾, meaning the caravan, which had no fighting in it. Ash-shawkah means harshness and strength, and it is also said to mean weapons.

﴿But Allah wished to establish the truth﴾, meaning: to make it manifest and to make it high, ﴿by His words﴾, meaning by His command to you to fight. It is also said [bi-'adawatihi] [[In manuscript A: (bi-'adawatihi).]], which preceded through the manifestation of the religion and its exaltation, ﴿and to cut off the last of the disbelievers﴾, meaning: to uproot them so that not one of them remains, namely the disbelievers of the Arabs.

﴿Li-yuḥiqqa al-ḥaqqa﴾ [so that He might establish the truth]: li-yuthabbita al-Islām (that He might make Islam firm). ﴿Wa-yubṭila al-bāṭila﴾ [and nullify falsehood]: i.e., yufnī al-kufr (that He might annihilate disbelief). ﴿Wa-law kariha al-mujrimūn﴾ [even if the criminals dislike it]: al-mushrikūn (the polytheists). The Battle of Badr took place on Friday, the morning of the seventeenth night of the month of Ramadan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Idh tastaghīthūna rabbakum﴾ [when you sought help from your Lord]: tastajīrūna bihi min ʿaduwwikum (you sought refuge with Him from your enemy) and taṭlubūna minhu al-ghawth wa-al-naṣr (you asked Him for aid and victory). It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: When the Day of Badr came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at the polytheists, who were a thousand, while his companions were three hundred and some ten men. He entered the ʿarīsh (hut), he and Abu Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him), and he faced the qiblah, stretched out his hand, and began calling upon his Lord, mighty and majestic: "O Allah, fulfil for me what You have promised me. O Allah, if You destroy this band of the people of Islam, You will not be worshipped on earth." He kept calling upon his Lord, mighty and majestic, extending his hands, until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr took his cloak and placed it back upon his shoulders, then embraced him from behind and said: "O Prophet of Allah, your earnest pleading with your Lord is enough, for He will surely fulfil for you what He has promised you." Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: "Idh tastaghīthūna rabbakum" [[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Jihad wa-al-Siyar, bab al-imdad bi-al-malaʾika fi ghazwat Badr (1763): 3/1383–1385; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/379.]] ﴿Fa-istajāba lakum annī mumiddukum﴾ [so He answered you: "I will reinforce you"], i.e., mursilun ilaykum madadan wa-ridan lakum (sending to you a reinforcement and a support for you), ﴿bi-alfin mina al-malāʾikati murdifīn﴾ [with a thousand of the angels, following one another].

The people of Medina and Yaʿqub read "murdafīn" with a fatḥah on the dāl (the letter dāl), meaning: Allah made the Muslims follow (ardafa Allah al-Muslimīn), and brought them as reinforcement. The others read it with a kasrah on the dāl, meaning: following one another in succession, one after another. It is said: ardaftuhu and radiftuhu (both) mean tabiʿtuhu (I followed him).

It is narrated that Jibril descended with five hundred, and Mikhaʾil with five hundred, in the form [ṣūrat] [[In "B": (ṣifa).]] of men, upon piebald horses, wearing white garments and white turbans on their heads, their ends let down between their shoulders [[Narrated by Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Mardawayh from Ibn ʿAbbas; see al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/27.]].

It is also narrated that when the Prophet (ﷺ) appealed to his Lord, mighty and majestic, and Abu Bakr said: "Indeed Allah will fulfil for you what He has promised you," the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dozed briefly while he was in the ʿarīsh, then awoke and said: "O Abu Bakr, the victory of Allah has come to you. This is Jibril, holding the rein of a horse, leading it over its ridges, with dust (rising)" [[A part of the previous hadith.]].

Abu ʿAbd Allah... [omitted]

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Naʿimi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated to us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, who said: ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated to us, who said: Khalid narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the Day of Badr: "This is Jibril, holding the head of his horse, wearing the equipment of war" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, bab shuhud al-malaʾika Badran: 7/312.]].

ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: The distinguishing marks (sīmā) of the angels on the Day of Badr were white turbans, and on the Day of Hunayn green turbans. The angels did not fight on any day other than the Day of Badr; on other days they were (only) a reinforcement and an aid in number [[Narrated by al-Tabarani as a statement of Ibn ʿAbbas (mawquf). It contains ʿAmmar ibn Abi Malik al-Janbi, whom al-Azdi declared weak; see Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid: 6/83.]] [145/a].

It is also related from Abu Usayd Malik ibn Rabiʿah, who witnessed Badr, that he said after his sight had gone: "If I were with you today at Badr, and my sight with me, I would have shown you the ravine from which the angels emerged" [[Attributed by al-Suyuti to Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/34.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 10–12:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And Allah did not make it﴾, meaning the reinforcement with angels, ﴿except as good tidings﴾, meaning as glad tidings, ﴿and so that your hearts might be reassured thereby. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Wise﴾.

﴿When He covered you with drowsiness﴾. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited "yaghshākum" with a fatḥa on the yā', and "al-nuʿās" (the drowsiness) is in the nominative case, because the verb has it as its subject, like His words in Surat Al 'Imran: "a security, drowsiness overcoming a group of you" [Al 'Imran: 154]. The people of Madina recited "yughshīkum" with a ḍamma on the yā' and a kasra on the shīn, lightly (mukhaffafan), and "al-nuʿās" is in the accusative, like His words: ﴿as if their faces had been covered﴾. The others recited with a ḍamma on the yā' and a kasra on the shīn, emphatically (mushaddadan), and "al-nuʿās" is in the accusative, the verb being for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, like His words: ﴿so He covered them with what covered them﴾ [al-Najm: 54]. And al-nuʿās is light sleep.

﴿Security﴾, meaning safety, ﴿from Him﴾. It is the verbal noun of amintu, amnan, amanatan and amanan. ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Drowsiness in battle is a security from Allah, and in prayer it is a whisper from Satan.

﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby﴾. This is because the Muslims alighted on the day of Badr upon a reddish sand dune in which feet and the hooves of animals sank, and the polytheists had preceded them to the water of Badr. The Muslims in the morning were some of them in a state of minor impurity and some in a state of major impurity (junub), thirst afflicted them, and Satan whispered to them, saying: "You claim that you are upon the truth, and that the Prophet of Allah is among you, and that you are the friends of Allah, yet the polytheists have overcome you for the water, and you pray in a state of minor and major impurity. How do you hope to prevail over them?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down upon them rain, from which the valley flowed. The believers drank, bathed, performed ablution, watered the mounts, and filled the water-skins. The dust was laid, the ground was packed so that feet could stand firm upon it, the whisper of Satan departed from them, and their souls were content. That is His words: ﴿And He sends down upon you water from the sky to purify you thereby﴾, from minor and major impurity.

﴿And to remove from you the defilement of Satan﴾, meaning his whisper, ﴿and to strengthen your hearts﴾ with certainty and patience, ﴿and to make firm the feet﴾, so that they do not sink into the sand, by the packing of the ground. It was also said: He makes the feet firm thereby through patience and strength of heart.

﴿When your Lord revealed to the angels﴾ whom He reinforced the believers with: ﴿that I am with you﴾ with help and victory, ﴿so strengthen those who have believed﴾, meaning: strengthen their hearts. It was said: That strengthening is their presence with them in the fighting and their assistance, meaning: strengthen them by your fighting alongside them against the polytheists.

Muqatil said: Meaning, give them glad tidings of victory. The angel would walk in front of the line in the form of a man, saying: "Rejoice, for Allah is your helper."

﴿I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾. Ata' said: He means fear of My friends. ﴿So strike above the necks﴾. It was said: This is an address to the believers. It was also said: This is an address to the angels, and it is connected to His words "so strengthen those who have believed." As for His words ﴿above the necks﴾, Ikrimah said: He means the heads, because they are above the necks. Al-Dahhak said: Its meaning is "strike the necks," and "fawq" is redundant (ṣila), as He said: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieved, then strike the necks﴾ [Muhammad: 4]. It was also said: Its meaning is "strike upon the necks," with "fawq" in the sense of "upon" (ʿalā).

﴿And strike from them every fingertip﴾. ʿAṭiyyah said: He means every joint. Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jurayj and al-Dahhak said: He means the extremities. Al-banān is the plural of banānah, which is the tips of the fingers of the two hands and the two feet. Ibn al-Anbari said: The angels did not know how human beings are killed, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, taught them.

We were informed by Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd al-Qadir al-Jurjani: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi told us, Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Juludi told us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan told us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj told us, Zuhayr ibn Harb told us, ʿAmr ibn Yunus al-Hanafi told us, ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmar told us, Abu Zumayl, who is Simak al-Hanafi, told us, ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAbbas told us, saying: "While a man from the Muslims that day was pursuing a man from the polytheists before him, he heard the sound of a whip above him and the voice of a horseman saying: 'Go forward, Hayzum!' Then he looked at the polytheist in front of him and he fell over on his back. He looked at him and his nose had been smashed and his face split, as by a whip-stroke, and all of it turned green. The Ansari came and related that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'You have spoken truly; that was from the reinforcement of the third heaven.'" They killed seventy of them that day and took seventy captive. [A fragment of the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas narrated by Muslim, mentioned above. "Hayzum" is the name of Gabriel's horse.]

It is related from Abu Dawud al-Mazini, who had witnessed Badr, that he said: "I was pursuing a man from the polytheists to strike him, when his head fell before my sword reached him, and I knew that someone other than me had killed him." [Narrated by ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Mardawayh. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/35–36.]

Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf related from his father, who said: "By Allah, we saw ourselves on the day of Badr, and one of us would point his sword at the polytheist, and his head would fall from his body before the sword reached him." [Attributed by al-Suyuti to Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh, 4/33.]

Ikrimah said: Abu Rafiʿ, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "I was a slave of al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him). Islam had entered our household: Umm al-Fadl had embraced Islam and I had embraced Islam, but al-ʿAbbas was in awe of his people and disliked opposing them, and he concealed his Islam. He was a man of abundant wealth scattered among his people. Abu Lahab, the enemy of Allah, had stayed behind from Badr and had sent in his place al-ʿAs ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughira. When the news of the calamity of the companions of Badr reached him, Allah humiliated and disgraced him. We found in ourselves strength and might. I was a weak man, and I used to make arrows and shape them in the chamber of Zamzam. By Allah, I was sitting shaping arrows, and Umm al-Fadl was sitting with me, when the wicked Abu Lahab came dragging his feet until he sat at the rope of the tent of the chamber (ṭunub, the rope of a tent, plural aṭnāb), so that his back was against my back. While he was sitting, the people said: 'This is Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, who has arrived.' Abu Lahab said: 'Come to me, my nephew, for you have the news.' He sat down with him while the people stood around him. He said: 'O my nephew, tell me how the affair of the people went.' He said: 'Nothing, by Allah. It was only that when we met them, they gave us their backs, killing us and taking us captive however they wished. And by Allah, despite that, I do not blame the people. We met white men upon piebald horses between the sky and the earth; by Allah, nothing could stand against them and nothing could withstand them.'" Abu Rafiʿ said: "I raised the rope of the chamber with my hand and said: 'By Allah, those were the angels!' Abu Lahab raised his hand and struck my face a severe blow. I grappled with him, and he seized me and threw me to the ground, then sat upon me striking me. I was a weak man, so Umm al-Fadl went to one of the pillars of the chamber, took it, and struck him with it, splitting a dreadful wound in his head. She said: 'Do you belittle him because his master is absent?' He got up, going away humiliated. By Allah, he did not live more than seven nights before Allah struck him with the plague (ʿadasah), and it killed him." [Narrated by al-Tabarani and al-Bazzar. Its chain contains Hasan ibn ʿAbdullah, whom Abu Hatim and others declared trustworthy, while a group declared him weak, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy. (Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/89).]

Miqsam related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The one who took al-ʿAbbas captive was Abu al-Yusr, Kaʿb ibn ʿAmr, of the Banu Salamah. Abu al-Yusr was a man of slight build, and al-ʿAbbas was a large man. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu al-Yusr: 'How did you take al-ʿAbbas captive?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a man helped me against him whom I had not seen before that nor after it, with such and such an appearance.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'A noble angel helped you against him.'" [Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/353. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma': 6/86, "Narrated by Ahmad, and in it is a narrator who is not named, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

**Surah 8, verses 13–16, from al-Baghawi's Commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil):**

﴿That is because they opposed Allah﴾ — they defied Allah, ﴿and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger – then indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

﴿That﴾ means: this punishment and blow which I have hastened upon you, O disbelievers, at Badr. ﴿So taste it﴾ — swiftly. ﴿And that for the disbelievers﴾ means: know and be certain that for the disbelievers there is a term in the Hereafter, ﴿the punishment of the Fire.﴾

ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished with Badr, it was said to him: "Go for the caravan; nothing stands in your way." Al-ʿAbbas, who was a captive in his bonds, called out: "It is not fitting." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Why?" He said: "Because Allah, the Exalted, promised you one of the two groups, and He has given you what He promised you."¹

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you meet those who have disbelieved advancing (zahfan)﴾ — that is, gathered, crowding one upon another. The ʿtazahuf' (تَزَاحُف) is drawing close in battle. The word zahf is a verbal noun (maṣdar); for this reason it is not pluralized, as in their saying: "a people ʿadl" and "riḍa." Al-Layth said: "The zahf is a group that advances toward its enemy all at once, so they are the zahf; the plural is zuhūf."

﴿So do not turn your backs to them﴾ — he says: do not turn your backs to them, that is, do not flee, for the one who flees turns his back.

﴿And whoever turns his back to them on that day﴾ — his back — ﴿except as one who swerves for battle﴾ — that is, one who wheels around, seeming to himself to be fleeing while his intention is to seek an opening, and he wants to return to the attack — ﴿or one who retreats to a company﴾ — that is, one who joins and goes over to a company of the believers, [intending] [[In manuscript "A": (intending).]] to return to fighting. The meaning of the verse is the prohibition of fleeing from the disbelievers and turning away from them, except with the intention of swerving for battle or joining a company of the Muslims so as to seek their help and return to the fight. Whoever turns his back without this intention incurs the threat, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿then he has returned with anger from Allah, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾

The scholars differed concerning this verse. Abu Saʿid al-Khudri said: "This applies specifically to the people of Badr. It was not permissible for them to flee, because the Prophet (ﷺ) was with them, and they had no company to retreat to apart from the Prophet (ﷺ). Had they retreated, they would have retreated to the polytheists. As for after that, the Muslims are a company for one another," so the fleeing person is one who retreats to a company, and his flight is not a grave sin. This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak.²

Yazid ibn Abi Habib said: "Allah made the Fire obligatory for whoever fled on the Day of Badr. Then, when the Day of Uhud came after that, He said: ʿIt was only Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned, and Allah has already pardoned them'" (Al ʿImran: 155). Then came the Day of Hunayn after it, and He said: ʿThen you turned back, retreating' (al-Tawbah: 25), ʿThen Allah relents after that to whom He wills' (al-Tawbah: 27).³

ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar said: "We were in an army which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent out, and the people were thrown into confusion (ḥāṣa ḥayṣatan) and we fled. We said: 'O Messenger of Allah, are we the fleeing ones?' He said: 'Rather, you are the ones who return to the attack; I am the company of the Muslims.'" ⁴

Muhammad ibn Sirin said: "When Abu ʿUbaydah was killed, the news reached ʿUmar, and he said: 'Had he retreated to me, I would have been a company for him, for I am a company for every Muslim.'"⁵

Some of them said: The ruling of the verse is general, concerning everyone who turns his back in flight. It has come in a hadith: "Fleeing from the advancing ranks (zahf) is one of the major sins."⁶

ʿAtaʾ ibn Abi Rabah said: "This verse is abrogated by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ʿNow Allah has lightened your burden' (al-Anfal: 66), so it is not permissible for a group to flee from [their equals] [[In manuscript "B": "their two times".]]. That ruling was abrogated except in this respect." The majority of the scholars hold this view: that when the Muslims are at least half of their enemy, it is not permissible for them to flee or turn their backs except as one who swerves for battle or retreats to a company; and if they are fewer than that, it is permissible for them to turn their backs and withdraw from them.⁷ Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Whoever flees from three has not fled; but whoever flees from two has fled."⁸

We cite here the preference of al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, that the verse is muhkam (established) and not abrogated, where he said in his Tafsir (13/440–441): "The more correct of the two interpretations of this verse in my view is the statement of the one who said: its ruling is established, and it was revealed concerning the people of Badr, and its ruling applies to all believers, and that Allah forbade the believers, when they meet the enemy, to turn their backs to them in flight, except to swerve for battle or to retreat to a company of the believers wherever it may be in the land of Islam; and that whoever turns his back to them after the advance (zahf) for battle, fleeing, without intending one of the two circumstances by which Allah permitted turning back, has deserved Allah's threat, unless He graciously pardons him. We say it is muhkam and not abrogated because, as we have shown in more than one place in this book and elsewhere, it is not permissible to rule that a verse is abrogated, while it has another meaning apart from abrogation, unless there is a proof that must be accepted—either a report that cuts off excuse, or a rational proof. And there is no proof of either kind that indicates the abrogation of the ruling of Allah's saying, Mighty and Majestic: ʿAnd whoever turns his back to them on that day—except as one who swerves for battle or retreats to a company.'"

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So you did not kill them, but it was Allah who killed them﴾. Mujahid said [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4 / 39.]] the occasion of revelation of this verse was that when they turned away from fighting, a man would say: "I killed so-and-so," and another would say the same, so the verse was revealed. Its meaning: you did not kill them by your own strength, but Allah killed them [by His help] [[In "B": (by His help).]] for you and by His strengthening of you.

It was also said: but Allah killed them by the reinforcement of the angels.

﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾. The people of tafsir and the military expeditions (maghazi) said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people (nadab, i.e., sent out and summoned them), so they set out until they alighted at Badr. The water-carriers of Quraysh came to them, and among them were Aslam, a black slave of the Banu al-Hajjaj, and Abu Yasar, a slave of the Banu al-'As ibn Sa'id. They brought both of them to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said to them: "Where is Quraysh?" They said: "They are behind this sand dune that you see, at the far edge of the valley" (al-kathib: al-'aqankal). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "How many are the people?" They said: "Many." He said: "What is their number?" They said: "We do not know." He said: "How many do they slaughter each day?" They said: "Ten one day and nine the next." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people are between nine hundred and a thousand." Then he said to them: "Who among them are the nobles of Quraysh?" They said: "'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham, Hakim ibn Hizam, al-Harith ibn 'Amir, Tu'aymah ibn 'Adi, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Nabih and Munabbih, the two sons of al-Hajjaj, and Suhayl ibn 'Amr." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is Makkah, which has thrown to you the falladh of its liver" [[Al-afladh: plural of fald, and fald is a piece (qit'ah); it is a metaphor meaning the essence and nobles of Quraysh, since the fald is among the noblest parts of the body. (From the margin of the tafsir).]]. When Quraysh advanced, and the Messenger of Allah saw them descending from the 'aqankal, which is the sand dune from which they came toward the valley, he said to them: "These are Quraysh, who have come with their arrogance and pride, opposing you [tuhaddu-ka] [[Tuhaddu-ka: tu'addi-ka. In "A": tujadil.]] and denying your Messenger. O Allah, grant me Your help which You promised me." Then Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and said: "Take a handful of dust and throw it at them." When the two hosts met, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a handful of pebbles mixed with dust, threw it into the faces of the people, and said: "May the faces be disfigured." Not a single polytheist remained but that some of it entered his eyes, his mouth and his nostrils. They fled, and the believers pursued them, killing and taking them captive [[See: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 1 / 616 onward (al-Halabi edition), and the Musnad of Imam Ahmad: 1 / 117.]].

Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: It has been related to us that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took three pebbles on the day of Badr, threw one at the right wing of the people, one at the left wing of the people, and one among them, and said: "May the faces be disfigured," and they fled. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw﴾, since no human is able to throw a handful of pebbles at the faces of an army such that no eye remains without being struck by something from it.

It was also said: the meaning of the verse is: "You did not convey when you threw, but Allah conveyed."

It was said: "You did not cast terror into their hearts when you threw the pebbles, but Allah cast terror into their hearts until they fled." ﴿And that He might bestow upon the believers a fine favour from Him﴾, i.e., that He might grant the believers a great blessing through victory and booty. ﴿Indeed Allah is All-Hearing﴾ of your supplication, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of your intentions.

﴿Dhalikum﴾ refers to what I mentioned: the killing, the shooting, and the good trial (al-bala' al-hasan). ﴿Wa-anna Allah﴾: it has been said that there is an implied element here, meaning [and know] (wa-a'lamu) that Allah is ﴿Muhin﴾, the one who weakens, ﴿kayd al-kafirin﴾ (the scheming of the disbelievers). Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and the people of Basra read "Muwahhin" with shaddah and tanwin, with "kayd" in the accusative. The others read "Muhin" without shaddah, with tanwin, except Hafs, who reads it as an annexed form (idafah), without tanwin, and puts "kayd" in the genitive.

God the Exalted says: ﴿If you seek a victory, then the victory has certainly come to you﴾. This is because Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr, when the two groups met: "O Allah, whichever of us has severed the ties of kinship and has come to us with what we do not recognise, destroy him this morning." So he was the one who sought victory against himself (al-mustaftih 'ala nafsihi). [See Sirat Ibn Hisham: 1/628. The meaning of "ahinhu" is "destroy him," and "al-mustaftih" is the one who judges against himself by this supplication.]

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Na'imi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: "I was in the row on the day of Badr, and I turned, and on my right and on my left were two young men of tender age. I felt uneasy in their presence. One of them said to me secretly from his companion: 'O uncle, show me Abu Jahl.' I said: 'O nephew, what will you do with him?' He said: 'I have sworn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that if I see him I will kill him or die before him.' The other said to me secretly from his companion the same thing. I was not pleased to be between two men like these. So I pointed them to him, and they rushed at him like two falcons until they struck him. They were the two sons of Afra'." [Related by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter "When they come close to you, shoot at them": 7/307-308, and Muslim in al-Jihad wa-al-Siyar, chapter "The entitlement of the killer to the spoils of the slain," no. (1752): 3/172.]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Na'imi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on a day: "Who will look for us what Abu Jahl has done?" He said: So Ibn Mas'ud set off and found him, the two sons of Afra' had struck him until he had gone cold. He said: So he took hold of his beard and said: "Are you Abu Jahl?" He said: "Is there anything above a man whom his people have killed, or whom you have killed?" [Related by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter "The killing of Abu Jahl": 7/293.]

[Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr related to me, saying: Mu'adh ibn Amr ibn al-Jamuh said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his expedition, he ordered that Abu Jahl ibn Hisham be searched for among the dead. He said: "O Allah, let him not escape You." He said: When I heard it, I made it my concern, so I went straight to him and struck him a blow that severed his foot (atannat qadamahu) at half his shin. [Atannat qadamahu: it cut off his foot.] He said: His son Ikrimah struck me on the shoulder, and my hand fell, and I hung by a piece of skin at my side. The fighting overwhelmed me (ajhadani al-qital), and I fought for most of my day, and I was dragging it behind me. When it troubled me, I put my foot on it, then I pulled it until I tore it off. Then he passed by Abu Jahl, who was mortally wounded ('aqir), Mu'awwidh ibn Afra', and struck him until he finished him, and left him with a last breath. Then Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud passed by Abu Jahl [from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham]. Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "I found him at his last breath, so I recognised him, and I placed my foot on his neck, then I said: 'Has Allah humiliated you, O enemy of Allah?' He said: 'With what has He humiliated me? Is a man whom you have killed greater than this? Tell me, to whom does the victory belong?' I said: 'To Allah and His Messenger.'" [al-Suhayli said in al-Rawd al-Unuf: 2/72: "That is, is there anything above a man whom his people have killed? This is the meaning of Ibn Hisham's explanation, where he said: that is, there is no shame upon him..."]

It is also narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: Abu Jahl said to me: "You have climbed a difficult height, O shepherd boy of the sheep." Then I cut off his head, and I brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the head of Abu Jahl." He said: "By Allah, other than whom there is no god?" I said: "Yes, by the One other than whom there is no god." Then I threw it before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he praised Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. [al-Suhayli also said: 2/72: "The Prophet's ﷺ saying: 'Allahu alladhi la ilaha illa huwa' (by Allah, other than whom there is no god) is in the genitive (bi-al-khafd) according to Sibawayh and others, because the interrogative stands in place of the governing preposition in his view. If you are informing, you say 'Allah' in the accusative, which al-Mubarrad does not permit anything other than. Sibawayh also permitted the genitive, because it is an oath, and it is known that the thing sworn by is governed by the preposition ba' or waw, and it is not permitted to omit the governing particle except in this position or in what is used very frequently, as it is narrated that Ru'ba used to say, when he was asked: 'How are you this morning?': 'Good, may Allah keep you well.'"]

Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: When the polytheists came out from Makkah to the Prophet ﷺ, they clung to the curtains of the Ka'bah and said: "O Allah, grant victory to the higher of the two armies, the more guided of the two groups, the more honourable of the two parties, and the better of the two religions." So it was concerning this that the verse was revealed: ﴿If you seek a victory, then the victory has certainly come to you﴾, meaning: if you seek help, then help has certainly come to you. [Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/453; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 269.]

Ikrimah said: The polytheists said: "By Allah, we do not know what Muhammad has brought, so decide between us and him with the truth." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿If you seek a victory, then the victory has certainly come to you﴾, meaning: if you seek a judgement, then the judgement has certainly come to you. [Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 269; Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/451; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/42.]

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: This is an address to the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Allah said to the Muslims: ﴿If you seek a victory, then the victory has certainly come to you﴾, meaning: if you seek help, then the victory and the help have certainly come to you.

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us, saying: Hajib ibn Ahmad informed us, saying: Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib related to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid related to us, from Qays, from Khabbab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: We complained to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reclining on a cloak of his in the shade of the Ka'bah, and we had met severe hardship from the polytheists. We said: "Will you not supplicate Allah for us? Will you not seek help for us?" So he sat up, his colour or his face reddened, and he said to us: "Among those before you, a man would be seized and a pit dug for him in the ground, then a saw would be brought and placed upon his head and he would be split in two, and that would not turn him from his religion. Iron combs would be used to rake the flesh from his bones and sinews, and that would not turn him from his religion. By Allah, this affair will certainly be completed, until a rider travels from Sana'a to Hadramawt fearing none but Allah, but you are hasty." [Related by al-Bukhari with similar wording, in al-Manaqib, chapter "The signs of prophethood in Islam": 6/619, and in Manaqib al-Ansar: 7/164-165. The author also mentioned it in Masabih al-Sunnah: 4/74.]

His saying: ﴿And if you cease﴾: he says to the disbelievers: if you cease from disbelief in Allah and from fighting His Prophet ﷺ, ﴿then it is better for you. And if you return﴾ to war against him and fighting him, ﴿We will return﴾ with the like of the event that befell you on the day of Badr. It has also been said: and if you return to supplication and seeking victory, We will return with victory for Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿And your company will not avail you anything, even if it is numerous﴾, meaning your group. ﴿And that Allah is with the believers﴾. The people of Madinah, Ibn Amir and Hafs read "wa-anna Allah" with a fathah on the hamzah, meaning: and because Allah is with the believers. Likewise: "your company will not avail you anything." It has also been said that it is a conjunction with His saying: "That, and that Allah weakens the scheming of the disbelievers." The others read "wa-inna Allah" with a kasrah on the alif, as a new sentence (ibtida').

The Almighty said: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him﴾, meaning, do not turn away from him, ﴿while you hear﴾ the Qur'an and its admonitions.

﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾, meaning: they say with their tongues, "We hear with our ears," while they do not hear, that is, they do not take heed and do not benefit from their hearing, so it is as if they had not heard.

The Almighty said: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and the dumb﴾ who are the worst of those who walk on the face of the earth [of Allah's creation] [[The text between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]], ﴿those who do not reason﴾ regarding the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. He called them "living creatures" (dawabb) because they benefit little from their intellects, as the Almighty said: ﴿They are like cattle; rather, they are even more astray﴾ [al-A'raf: 179]. Ibn 'Abbas said: They were a group from the Banu 'Abd al-Dar ibn Qusayy, who used to say, "We are deaf, dumb, and blind to what Muhammad brings." They were all killed at Uhud, and they were the standard-bearers. Only two of them embraced Islam: Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr and Suwaybit ibn Harmala.

﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear﴾, meaning, He would have made them hear with understanding and acceptance. ﴿And even if He had made them hear﴾ after He knew that there was no good in them, they would not have benefited from it, ﴿they would have turned away while being averse﴾, due to their obstinacy and their denial of the truth after it had become clear. It was also said: They used to say to the Prophet (ﷺ), "Resurrect Qusayy for us, for he was a blessed elder, so that he may bear witness to your prophethood, and then we will believe in you." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "And if He had made them hear" the speech of Qusayy, "they would have turned away while being averse."

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "And if He had made them hear" the speech of Qusayy, "they would have turned away while being averse."

The Almighty said: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not turn away from him﴾, meaning, do not turn away from him, ﴿while you hear﴾ the Qur'an and its admonitions.

﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾, meaning: they say with their tongues, "We hear with our ears," while they do not hear, that is, they do not take heed and do not benefit from their hearing, so it is as if they had not heard.

The Almighty said: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and the dumb﴾ who are the worst of those who walk on the face of the earth [of Allah's creation] [[The text between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]], ﴿those who do not reason﴾ regarding the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. He called them "living creatures" (dawabb) because they benefit little from their intellects, as the Almighty said: ﴿They are like cattle; rather, they are even more astray﴾ [al-A'raf: 179]. Ibn 'Abbas said: They were a group from the Banu 'Abd al-Dar ibn Qusayy, who used to say, "We are deaf, dumb, and blind to what Muhammad brings." They were all killed at Uhud, and they were the standard-bearers. Only two of them embraced Islam: Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr and Suwaybit ibn Harmala.

﴿And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear﴾, meaning, He would have made them hear with understanding and acceptance. ﴿And even if He had made them hear﴾ after He knew that there was no good in them, they would not have benefited from it, ﴿they would have turned away while being averse﴾, due to their obstinacy and their denial of the truth after it had become clear. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 24–25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾. He says: respond to both of them with obedience. ﴿When he calls you﴾: the Messenger (ﷺ). ﴿To that which gives you life﴾: i.e., to that which gives you life. Al-Suddi said: it is faith, for the disbeliever is dead, so he is given life through faith.

Qatadah said: it is the Qur'an, in which is life, by which is salvation, and protection in both abodes.

Mujahid said: it is the truth.

Ibn Ishaq said: it is jihad, through which Allah honoured you after humiliation.

Al-Qutaybi said: rather, it is martyrdom. Allah, may He be exalted, said concerning the martyrs: ﴿Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ (Al 'Imran 3:169).

It has been related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was praying, and called him. Ubayy hastened in his prayer, then came, and the Messenger of Allah said: "What prevented you from responding to me when I called you?" He said: "I was in prayer." He said: "Does not Allah, mighty and majestic, say: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life﴾?" [He said: "Indeed, O Messenger of Allah, I will not fail to respond to you whenever you call me, even if I am praying."] [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir 13/467 with this wording. Similar was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Qur'an, chapter on the virtue of Surat al-Fatihah, 8/178–180, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. Also Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 2/412–413. Al-Bukhari narrated it with a different context in the Tafsir, 8/156, and in Fada'il al-Qur'an. Al-Mundhiri said: Ibn Khuzaymah and Ibn Hibban narrated it in their Sahihs, and al-Hakim in abridged form, from Abu Hurayrah from Ubayy; al-Hakim said: sahih according to the condition of Muslim. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi pp. 68–69; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi 8/180.] [The text between the brackets is from manuscript "B".]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And know that Allah comes between a person and his heart﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ata said: He comes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith.

Al-Dahhak said: He comes between the disbeliever and obedience, and comes between the believer and disobedience.

Mujahid said: He comes between a person and his heart, so he does not understand and does not know what he does.

Al-Suddi said: He comes between a person and his heart, so he is unable to believe or to disbelieve except by His permission.

It was also said: this refers to the fact that when the people were called to fight in a state of weakness, their thoughts became bad and their breasts were troubled, so it was said to them: fight in the way of Allah, and know that Allah comes between a person and his heart, so He turns fear into security and cowardice into courage.

﴿And that to Him you will be gathered﴾, so that He will recompense you for your deeds.

We were informed by Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us, who said: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Hammad narrated to us, who said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah used often to say: "O Turner of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have believed in you and in what you brought; do you fear for us?" He said: "The hearts are between two fingers of the fingers of Allah; He turns them." [Narrated with this wording by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 3/112, 257; al-Tirmidhi with the addition "however He wills" in Qadr, chapter on what has come that the hearts are between two fingers of the fingers of the Merciful, 6/349; and Muslim from the narration of Abdullah ibn Amr, in Qadr, chapter on Allah's turning of hearts however He wills, no. 2654, 4/2045. Al-Baghawi also mentioned it in Masabih al-Sunnah 1/141.]

His saying: ﴿And beware of a trial﴾, that is, a test and an affliction, ﴿which will not strike especially those of you who have wronged﴾. His saying "which will not strike" is not a pure conditional; if it were a conditional, the nun (emphatic particle) would not enter it. Rather, it is [a prohibition] [[In "A" (nahy, prohibition).]], and it contains an element of the conditional, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings lest Solomon and his armies crush you﴾ (al-Naml 27:18). Its implied meaning is: "And beware of a trial; if you do not guard against it, it will strike you." It is like the saying of one who says: "Get down from the animal, lest it throw you down," which is the answer to the command expressed in the form of a prohibition; its meaning is: "If you get down, it will not throw you."

The exegetes said: this verse was revealed concerning the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and its meaning is: beware of a trial that strikes the wrongdoer and the non-wrongdoer alike.

Al-Hasan said: it was revealed concerning Ali, Ammar, Talhah and al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them. al-Zubayr said: "We recited this verse for a long time and did not think that we were among its people; then we turned out to be those meant by it," meaning on the day of the Battle of the Camel. [Tafsir al-Tabari 13/472–473, where it says: it was revealed concerning Ali, Ammar and Talhah...]

Al-Suddi, Muqatil, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: this refers to particular people among the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) whom the trial afflicted on the day of the Camel. [Tafsir al-Tabari 13/473.]

Ibn Abbas said: Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded the believers not to tolerate wrongdoing among them, lest Allah encompass them all with a punishment that strikes the wrongdoer and the non-wrongdoer. [Tafsir al-Tabari 13/474, without the phrase "strikes the wrongdoer and the non-wrongdoer."]

We were informed by Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah, who said: Abu Tahir al-Harithi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i informed us, who said: Abdullah ibn Mahmud informed us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Khallal informed us, who said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sayf ibn Abi Sulayman, who said: I heard Adi ibn Adi al-Kindi say: a client of ours narrated to me that he heard my grandfather say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed Allah does not punish the common folk for the deeds of the elite, until they see wrongdoing among them while they are able to forbid it and do not forbid it. When they do that, Allah punishes both the common folk and the elite." [Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 4/192; al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar 2/66; Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, no. 1352, p. 476; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 14/346.] Al-Zayd (Ibn Zayd) said: by the trial is meant the scattering of the word and the opposition of some of them to others. [Compare his other statement in al-Tabari 13/475, where he said: the trial is misguidance.]

We were informed by Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi, who said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, who said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, who said: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Trials will occur in which the one sitting is better than the one standing, the one standing is better than the one walking, and the one walking is better than the one running. Whoever lifts his head toward them, they will lift it toward him. So whoever finds a refuge or a shelter, let him seek refuge in it." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Fitan, chapter on the occurrence of trials, the one sitting therein is better than the one standing, 13/29, and in al-Anbiya', and al-Manaqib; Muslim in al-Fitan, chapter on the descent of trials like the falling of rain, no. 2886, 4/2212; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 15/22.]

His saying: ﴿Do not let the trial strike those who have wronged among you in particular﴾, meaning: the punishment. ﴿And know that Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 26:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land﴾. He says: Remember, O company of the emigrants (muhajirun), when you were few in number and oppressed in the land of Makkah at the beginning of Islam. ﴿You feared that the people would snatch you away﴾, that people would carry you off, meaning the disbelievers of Makkah. ʿIkrimah said: the disbelievers of the Arabs. Wahb said: Persia and Rome. ﴿So He sheltered you﴾ in Madinah. ﴿And strengthened you with His help﴾, that is, He strengthened you on the day of Badr through the Ansar. al-Kalbi said: He strengthened you on the day of Badr through the angels. ﴿And provided for you of the good things﴾, meaning the spoils of war, which He made lawful for you and did not make lawful for anyone before you. ﴿That perhaps you may be grateful﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 27–28:

﴿O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger﴾ Al-Suddi said: They would hear something from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and divulge it, until it reached the polytheists [[al-Tabari: 13/483.]].

Al-Zuhri and al-Kalbi said: The verse was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah, Harun ibn Abd al-Mundhir al-Ansari, of the Banu Awf ibn Malik. This was because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ besieged the Jews of Qurayzah for twenty-one nights. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to make peace on the same terms on which their brothers, the Banu al-Nadir, had made peace, namely that they would go to their brothers in Adhri'at and Ariha, in the land of Syria. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ refused to grant them that, unless they came down under the judgement of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh. They refused and said: "Send Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir to us," for he was a sincere adviser to them, since his property, his children and his dependants were with them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him, and he came to them. They said to him: "O Abu Lubabah, do you think we should come down under the judgement of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh?" Abu Lubabah pointed with his hand to his throat, indicating that it meant slaughter, "so do not do it." Abu Lubabah said: "By Allah, my feet had not moved from their places before I realised that I had betrayed Allah and His Messenger." Then he set off on his face and did not go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he tied himself to one of the pillars of the mosque and said: "By Allah, I will not taste food or drink until I die or Allah accepts my repentance." When news of him reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "If he had come to me, I would have asked forgiveness for him. But since he has done what he has done, I will not release him until Allah accepts his repentance." He remained for seven days, tasting no food or drink, until he fell unconscious. Then Allah accepted his repentance. It was said to him: "O Abu Lubabah, your repentance has been accepted." He said: "No, by Allah, I will not free myself until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the one who frees me." So he (ﷺ) came and untied him with his own hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: "O Messenger of Allah, part of the completion of my repentance is that I abandon the house of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I strip myself of all my wealth." The Prophet ﷺ said: "A third will suffice you, so give it in charity." So the verse "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger" was revealed concerning him [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/481; Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 2/237–238; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi pp. 269–270; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/48–49.]].

﴿and betray your trusts﴾, meaning: [and do not betray your trusts] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] ﴿while you know﴾ that they are trusts. It was also said: "while you know" that what you did, namely the gesture towards the throat, was betrayal.

Al-Suddi said: When they betray Allah and the Messenger, they have betrayed their trusts.

Ibn Abbas said: Do not betray Allah by abandoning His obligations, nor the Messenger by abandoning his Sunnah, and do not betray your trusts.

Ibn Abbas also said: Trusts are those obligations of Allah that are hidden from the eyes of people, and the deeds for which Allah has entrusted them.

Qatadah said: Know that the religion of Allah is a trust, so discharge to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, what He has entrusted to you of His obligations and limits, and whoever has a trust upon him, let him discharge it to the one who entrusted him with it.

﴿And know that your wealth and your children are a trial﴾ It was said: This too was about Abu Lubabah, because his wealth and children were among the Banu Qurayzah, and so he said what he said out of fear for them.

It was also said: This applies to all people. Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, by dictation, and Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi informed us, both said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Isfara'ini informed us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn [Razmawayh] [[In "B": (Dharqawayh).]] narrated to us, Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Ghalib narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us from Abu al-Aswad, from Urwah, from Aisha, that the Prophet ﷺ was brought a child, and he kissed it and said: "Indeed they are a cause of miserliness and cowardice, and indeed they are among the fragrant herbs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic" [[Narrated by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/35, in which is Ibn Lahi'ah, who had a weak memory; the hadith has supporting reports that strengthen it, in Ahmad: 6/409, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Birr wa al-Silah.]].

﴿And that with Allah is a great reward﴾ for those who advise Allah and His Messenger and discharge their trust.
