So the verse "Do not betray Allah and the Messenger" was revealed concerning him [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 13/481; Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 2/237–238; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi pp. 269–270; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/48–49.]].

﴿and betray your trusts﴾, meaning: [and do not betray your trusts] [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] ﴿while you know﴾ that they are trusts. It was also said: "while you know" that what you did, namely the gesture towards the throat, was betrayal.

Al-Suddi said: When they betray Allah and the Messenger, they have betrayed their trusts.

Ibn Abbas said: Do not betray Allah by abandoning His obligations, nor the Messenger by abandoning his Sunnah, and do not betray your trusts.

Ibn Abbas also said: Trusts are those obligations of Allah that are hidden from the eyes of people, and the deeds for which Allah has entrusted them.

Qatadah said: Know that the religion of Allah is a trust, so discharge to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, what He has entrusted to you of His obligations and limits, and whoever has a trust upon him, let him discharge it to the one who entrusted him with it.

﴿And know that your wealth and your children are a trial﴾ It was said: This too was about Abu Lubabah, because his wealth and children were among the Banu Qurayzah, and so he said what he said out of fear for them.

It was also said: This applies to all people. Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, by dictation, and Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi informed us, both said: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Isfara'ini informed us, Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn [Razmawayh] [[In "B": (Dharqawayh).]] narrated to us, Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Ghalib narrated to us, Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us from Abu al-Aswad, from Urwah, from Aisha, that the Prophet ﷺ was brought a child, and he kissed it and said: "Indeed they are a cause of miserliness and cowardice, and indeed they are among the fragrant herbs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic" [[Narrated by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/35, in which is Ibn Lahi'ah, who had a weak memory; the hadith has supporting reports that strengthen it, in Ahmad: 6/409, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Birr wa al-Silah.]].

﴿And that with Allah is a great reward﴾ for those who advise Allah and His Messenger and discharge their trust.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿O you who have believed, if you fear Allah﴾ by obeying Him and abandoning disobedience to Him, ﴿He will grant you a criterion (furqan)﴾.

Mujahid said: a way out (makhraj) in this world and the Hereafter.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: a way out in religion from doubtful matters (shubuhat).

Ikrimah said: deliverance (najah), meaning He will separate for you between you and what you fear.

Ad-Dahhak said: clarification (bayan). Ibn Ishaq said: a distinction between truth and falsehood, by which Allah makes your truth manifest and extinguishes the falsehood of those who oppose you. And al-Furqan is a verbal noun (masdar) like ar-Rujhan (the outweighing) and an-Nuqsan (the diminishing).

﴿And He will remove from you your misdeeds﴾, meaning He will erase from you what has passed of your sins, ﴿and forgive you. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 30:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾. This verse is connected [to what came before it] [[In "B": (to what precedes it).]] ﴿And remember when you were few﴾, meaning: "And remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you, and when they said, 'O Allah...'" This is because this surah is Medinan, and this plotting and saying took place in Makkah. But Allah reminded them of it in Medina, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If you do not support him, Allah has already supported him﴾ (At-Tawbah 9:40). This plotting, as Ibn Abbas and others among the people of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) reported, was as follows:

When the Ansar embraced Islam, Quraysh feared that the affair of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would grow strong. So a group of their elders gathered in Dar al-Nadwah to consult about the affair of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Their leaders were Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Abu Sufyan, Tu'aymah ibn Adi, Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham, Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad, Hakim ibn Hizam, Nubayh and Munabbih, the two sons of al-Hajjaj, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf. Iblis confronted them in the form of an old man. When they saw him, they said, "Who are you?" He said, "An old man from Najd. I heard of your gathering, so I wished to attend, and you will not lack opinion and counsel from me." They said, "Enter," so he entered.

Abu al-Bakhtari said, "As for me, I think you should take Muhammad and imprison him in a room, bind his chains, and seal the door of the room except for an opening through which you cast him his food and drink, and wait for the vicissitudes of fate (rayb al-manun) to befall him until he dies there, just as those poets before him died."

The old man of Najd cried out, the enemy of Allah, and said, "Evil is the opinion you have held! By Allah, if you imprison him in a room, his affair will go out from behind the door you have closed upon him to his companions, and they will soon attack you, fight you, and take him from your hands."

They said, "The old man has spoken truly."

Hisham ibn Amr of the Banu Amir ibn Lu'ayy said, "As for me, I think you should load him onto a camel and expel him from among you. Then what he does and where he goes will not harm you, once he has left you and you are rid of him."

Iblis said, "This is not an opinion for you to rely upon. You intend a man who has corrupted your minds, and you would expel him to others, who would then be corrupted by him. Have you not seen the sweetness of his speech, the sweetness of his tongue, and how he captivates hearts with what you hear from his words? By Allah, if you do that, he will go and win over the hearts of a people, then he will march with them against you and drive you out of your lands."

They said, "The old man has spoken truly."

Abu Jahl said, "By Allah, I will give you an opinion that I think is the only one. I think you should take from every clan of Quraysh a young man of noble lineage, strong and vigorous, then give each youth of them a sharp sword, and then they should strike him with one blow as one man. When they have killed him, his blood will be dispersed among all the tribes, and I do not think the Banu Hashim will be able to fight all of Quraysh. When they see that, they will accept the blood-money (al-'aql), and Quraysh will pay his diyah (blood-money)."

Iblis said, "This young man has spoken truly. He is the best of you in opinion. The matter is as he has said. I see no opinion other than it."

So they dispersed according to the opinion of Abu Jahl, and they were all in agreement on it.

Then Jibril came to the Prophet (ﷺ), informed him of that, and commanded him not to sleep in the bed in which he used to sleep. Allah then permitted him to leave for Medina. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded Ali ibn Abi Talib to sleep in his bed, and said to him, "Wrap yourself in this cloak of mine, for no harm that you dislike will reach you from them." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) went out, took a handful of dust, and Allah blinded their sight to him. He began to scatter the dust over their heads while reciting: ﴿Indeed, We have placed shackles upon their necks﴾ up to His saying ﴿so they cannot see﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin 36:8-9) [147/b]. He went to the cave of Thawr with Abu Bakr, and he left Ali in Makkah so that he could return the trusts (al-wada'i') that had been entrusted to him, for trusts used to be deposited with the Prophet (ﷺ) because of his truthfulness and trustworthiness.

The polytheists spent the night guarding Ali in the bed of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), thinking that he was the Prophet (ﷺ). When they rose in the morning, they rushed at him and found Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. They said, "Where is your companion?" He said, "I do not know." So they followed his tracks and sent people in pursuit of him. When they reached the cave, they saw spider webs over its entrance, and they said, "Had he entered it, there would not have been spider webs over its entrance." He remained in it for three days, then he came to Medina. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you﴾ [[See: al-Tabari: 13/496 and following, with the commentary of Shaykh Mahmud Shakir; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/27; al-Durr al-Manthur 4/51-52.]].

﴿To restrain you﴾: to imprison you, confine you, and bind you. ﴿Or kill you or expel you﴾. ﴿And they plot, and Allah plots﴾. Al-Dahhak said: "They devise, and Allah devises." And al-makr (plotting) is planning; and when it comes from Allah, it is planning with truth. It was also said: He will repay them with the recompense of their plotting. ﴿And Allah is the best of planners﴾.

al-Baghawi's commentary (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 8, verse 31:

﴿When Our verses are recited to them, they say﴾: meaning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith. ﴿We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this.﴾

The reason for this is that he used to travel as a merchant to Persia and al-Hirah, where he would hear the reports of Rustam and Isfandiyar and the tales of the non-Arabs (*al-'Ajam*). He would also pass by the Jews and Christians and see them reading the Torah and the Gospel and bowing and prostrating. When he came to Makkah, he found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) praying and reciting the Qur'an, and al-Nadr said: "We have heard; if we willed, we could say the like of this." [[See: al-Tabari: 13/503–504; al-Wahidi, *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. 270; al-Suyuti, *al-Durr al-Manthur*: 4/55.]] ﴿This is nothing but the myths of the ancients (asatir al-awwalin).﴾ That is, the reports of the past nations and their names, and what the ancients inscribed in their books.

"Asatir" is the plural of "ustura" (fable, myth), which means that which is written, from their saying *sutirat*, meaning it was written. [[See: al-Tabari: 11/308–310; 13/503.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 32–33:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is the truth from You"﴾ — the verse. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith from the Banu Abd al-Dar [[Tafsir al-Tabari 13/505–506; al-Durr al-Manthur 4/55.]].

Ibn Abbas said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recounted the stories of the previous generations, al-Nadr said: "If I wished, I could say the like of this. This is nothing but the fables of the ancients" — that is, this is nothing but what the ancients recorded in their books. Uthman ibn Maz'un (may Allah be pleased with him) said to him: "Fear Allah, for Muhammad speaks the truth." He said: "I too speak the truth." Uthman said: "Muhammad says, 'There is no god but Allah.'" He said: "I too say, 'There is no god but Allah, but these are the daughters of Allah'" — meaning the idols. Then he said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You" — "al-Haqq" is in the accusative as the predicate of kana, and the pronoun (huwa) is an 'imad (supporting pronoun) and a silah (connective) — "then rain down on us stones from the heaven" as You rained them upon the people of Lut, "or bring us a painful punishment" — that is, with some of the punishments by which You punished the nations. And concerning him was revealed: "A questioner asked about a punishment that will befall" [al-Ma'arij: 1] [[See al-Durr al-Manthur 8/277.]].

Ata said: Some ten-odd verses were revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, and what he asked for in punishment befell him on the day of Badr [[al-Durr al-Manthur 8/278.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed three from Quraysh by way of sabr (execution after capture) on the day of Badr: Tu'aymah ibn Adi, Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'it, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf 14/372, and Abu Ubayd in al-Amwal (154), from the route of Hushaym from Abu Bishr, where it reads "Mut'im ibn Adi" instead of "Tu'aymah." He then said: "This is Hushaym's narration; but the scholars of the maghazi (military expeditions) deny the killing of Mut'im ibn Adi, saying: he died in Makkah before Badr, and it was his brother Tu'aymah ibn Adi who was killed, not by sabr, but in the battle." Among what confirms their view is the hadith from al-Zuhri that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Jubayr ibn Mut'im, when he spoke to him about the captives: "Had the old man (meaning his father Mut'im ibn Adi) come to us, we would have interceded for him." So how could he have been killed that day when the Prophet (ﷺ) said this about him? As for the killing of Uqbah and al-Nadr, there is no disagreement about it." (al-Amwal of Abu Ubayd, pp. 154–155).]].

Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the one who said it was Abu Jahl.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Nadr narrated to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid, the companion of al-Ziyadi, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Jahl said: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the heaven, or bring us a painful punishment." So there was revealed: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you were among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness. And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them?﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, chapter: "And when they said, 'O Allah, if this is the truth'," 8/308.]].

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you were among them﴾ — the scholars differed about the meaning of this verse. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: This is a report about the polytheists, that they said it, and it is connected to the first verse. That is because they used to say, "Allah will not punish us while we seek His forgiveness, and He does not punish a nation while its prophet is with it." So Allah, exalted is He, said to His Prophet (ﷺ), mentioning their ignorance, their delusion, and their seeking of victory against themselves: "And when they said, 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You'" — the verse. And they said: ﴿But Allah would not punish them while you were among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. Then He said in rebuttal to them: ﴿And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them?﴾, and even though you are among them and even though they seek forgiveness, "while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram" [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 13/512–513.]].

Others said: This is a new (independent) statement, in which Allah, mighty and majestic, informs about Himself: "But Allah would not punish them."

They differed about its interpretation. Al-Dahhak and a group said: its interpretation is: "But Allah would not punish them while you are among them," remaining among them. They said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was residing in Makkah; then he left from among them, and a remnant of the Muslims remained there seeking forgiveness. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾. Then those [Muslims] left from among them and were punished, and Allah permitted the conquest of Makkah; that is the punishment He had promised them [[al-Tabari: 13/510–511.]].

Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: Allah does not punish a town until the Prophet and those who believe leave it and go to the place where he was commanded. So He said: "But Allah would not punish them while you were among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness" [[al-Tabari: 13/511.]] — meaning the Muslims. When they left, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them?﴾, and Allah punished them on the day of Badr.

Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said: There were two securities among you: "But Allah would not punish them while you were among them" and "nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness." As for the Prophet (ﷺ), he has passed away, and the seeking of forgiveness remains among you until the Day of Resurrection [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir: 8/472–473, as a marfu' report, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith, and Isma'il ibn Ibrahim is weak in narrations." It is also narrated by al-Tabari as a mawquf report from Abu Musa: 13/513.]].

Some of them said: This seeking of forgiveness refers to the polytheists, for they used to say after the tawaf: "Ghufranaka, ghufranaka" (We seek Your forgiveness) [[al-Tabari: 13/511.]].

Yazid ibn Ruman said: The Quraysh said, "If this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the heaven." When evening came, they regretted what they had said, and said, "Ghufranaka, O Allah." So Allah, mighty and majestic, said: "But Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness" [[al-Tabari: 13/512.]].

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: Its meaning is: "And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness," that is, if they had sought forgiveness; but they were not seeking forgiveness. And if they had acknowledged the sin and sought forgiveness, they would have been believers [[al-Tabari: 13/514.]].

It was said: This is a call to Islam and to seeking forgiveness through this word, like a man who says to another, "I will not punish you while you obey me," meaning: obey me so that I do not punish you.

Mujahid and Ikrimah said: "While they seek forgiveness" means "while they submit (to Islam)." It is said: If they had submitted, they would not have been punished [[al-Tabari: 13/515.]]. Al-Walibi related from Ibn Abbas: That is, among them are those for whom it was already decreed by Allah that they would submit, believe, and seek forgiveness [[al-Tabari: 13/516.]]; such as Abu Sufyan, Safwan ibn Umayyah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Suhayl ibn Amr, Hakim ibn Hizam, and others.

Abd al-Wahhab related from Mujahid: "while they seek forgiveness" means: in their loins there are those who will seek forgiveness.

[[Al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 13/517: "The most correct of these views in my opinion is the view of the one who said: its interpretation is: 'And Allah would not punish them while you, O Muhammad, are among them, remaining among them, until I bring you out from among them, for I do not destroy a town in which is its prophet.' 'Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness' from their sins and their disbelief; but they do not seek forgiveness from that, rather they persist in it, so they deserve the punishment." Then it is said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram?" meaning: what is their situation, and what prevents Allah from punishing them, when they do not seek Allah's forgiveness for their disbelief so that they might believe in Him, and they bar the believers in Allah and His Messenger from al-Masjid al-Haram?]].

[[Al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: 13/517: "The most correct of these views in my opinion is the view of the one who said: its interpretation is: 'And Allah would not punish them while you, O Muhammad, are among them, remaining among them, until I bring you out from among them, for I do not destroy a town in which is its prophet.' 'Nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness' from their sins and their disbelief; but they do not seek forgiveness from that, rather they persist in it, so they deserve the punishment." Then it is said: "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them, while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram?" meaning: what is their situation, and what prevents Allah from punishing them, when they do not seek Allah's forgiveness for their disbelief so that they might believe in Him, and they bar the believers in Allah and His Messenger from al-Masjid al-Haram?]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 34–35:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them﴾, meaning: what prevents them from being punished, intending after your departure from among them, ﴿while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram﴾, meaning: they prevent the believers from circumambulating the House.

It was also said: by the first punishment he meant the punishment of annihilation (isti'sal), and by his saying "And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them" he meant: by the sword.

It was also said: by the first he meant the punishment of this world, and by this verse the punishment of the Hereafter.

Al-Hasan said: the first verse, which is His saying: "And Allah would not punish them", is abrogated (mansukha) by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them﴾ [[Imam al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "There is no basis for the view of those who say that this is abrogated by His saying: 'And what is [the matter] with them that Allah should not punish them while they bar [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram', because His saying, majestic is His praise, 'And Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness' is a report (khabar), and a report cannot contain abrogation; abrogation applies only to a command or a prohibition." Al-Tafsir: 13/518.]].

﴿And they were not its guardians﴾. Al-Hasan said: the polytheists used to say, "We are the guardians of al-Masjid al-Haram," so Allah refuted them with His saying: "And they were not its guardians", meaning: the guardians of the House. ﴿Its guardians are only the pious﴾, meaning: the believers who guard against shirk. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And their prayer at the House was not but whistling and clapping﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan said: al-mukaa' is whistling; linguistically it is also the name of a white bird found in the Hijaz which has a whistle, as if he said: "except the sound of a mukaa'". And al-tasdiyah is clapping.

Ibn 'Abbas said: the Quraysh used to circumambulate the House while naked, whistling and clapping.

Mujahid said: each group of the Banu 'Abd al-Dar would confront the Prophet ﷺ during the circumambulation, mocking him, and would put their fingers into their mouths and whistle. So al-mukaa' is placing the fingers in the cheek, and al-tasdiyah is whistling, and from it comes al-sada, the echo that the one who calls out hears in the mountain.

Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah said: I asked Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman about His saying, majestic is He, "except whistling and clapping", and he joined his palms and then blew into them a whistle.

Muqatil said: whenever the Prophet ﷺ prayed in the mosque, two men would stand on his right and whistle, and two men on his left and clap, so as to confuse the Prophet's ﷺ prayer; and they were from the Banu 'Abd al-Dar.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: al-tasdiyah is their barring the believers from al-Masjid al-Haram, and from the religion and the prayer. On this interpretation it is originally al-tasdidah with two dals, and one of the two dals was changed into a yaa', as is said: tazannaytu from al-zann, and taqada al-bazi when the falcon broke (its wing), meaning taqadqada al-bazi. Ibn al-Anbari said: he called it a prayer only because they were commanded to pray in the mosque, so they made that their prayer.

﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve﴾

﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve﴾

The Words of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to turn (people) away from the way of Allah﴾ means: to divert (people) from the religion of Allah.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning those who fed (others) on the day of Badr. They were twelve men: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, 'Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah ibn 'Abd Shams, Nabih and Munabbih, the two sons of al-Hajjaj, Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Hakim ibn Hizam, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad, al-Harith ibn 'Amir ibn Nawfal, and al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. All of them were from Quraysh, and each one of them used to feed (people) ten camels every day [See: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 1/671; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 271].

Al-Hakam ibn 'Uyaynah said: It was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan, who spent forty uqiyyah (on the polytheists) on the day of Uhud [See: al-Tabari: 13/531; Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 272; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/63].

The Exalted said: ﴿Then they will spend it, and then it will become a regret for them﴾, meaning: what they spent in this world will become a regret for them in the Hereafter. ﴿Then they will be overcome﴾, and will not prevail. ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾ among them ﴿to Hell they will be gathered﴾. The disbelievers were singled out because some of them embraced Islam.

﴿That Allah may distinguish the wicked﴾ [in the way of Satan] [[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "B".]] ﴿from the good﴾. This means the disbeliever from the believer, so that He places the believer in the Gardens and the disbeliever in the Fires.

Al-Kalbi said: "The wicked deed is distinguished from the righteous good deed, so that for the righteous deeds He gives Paradise, and for the wicked deeds the Fire."

It has also been said: "This means the wicked spending in the way of Satan, as distinct from the good spending in the way of Allah."

﴿And He places the wicked, some of it upon others﴾, meaning, one piled upon another, ﴿and heaps it all together﴾, meaning He gathers it. From this comes the phrase "heaped clouds" (al-sahab al-markum), which is the dense, compacted mass. ﴿Then He puts it into Hell﴾. ﴿They are the losers﴾. This refers back to His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth...﴾ . . .

﴿They are the losers﴾, those whose trade has failed, because they exchanged their wealth for the punishment of the Hereafter.

﴿Say to those who disbelieve: If they desist﴾ from polytheism, ﴿they will be forgiven what has already passed﴾, meaning their sins before Islam. ﴿But if they return, the precedent of the former peoples has already passed﴾, referring to Allah's custom of granting victory to His prophets and destroying their enemies.

Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi said: "It is a monotheism that is not unable to demolish the disbelief that preceded it. I hope it will not be unable to demolish the sin that follows it."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 39–41 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah,﴾ that is, shirk (associating others with God). Al-Rabi' said: "Until no believer is tempted away from his religion." ﴿And religion is entirely for Allah,﴾ that is, religion becomes purely for Allah, with no shirk in it. ﴿But if they cease﴾ from disbelief, ﴿then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ Ya'qub read "ta'malun" (with a ta' at the beginning, addressing them), while the others read it with a ya' ("ya'malun").

﴿But if they turn away﴾ from faith and return to fighting its people, ﴿then know that Allah is your Protector (mawlakum),﴾ your Helper and Supporter, ﴿an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of any spoils (ghanimtum min shay'),﴾ ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it,﴾ and so on. Al-ghanimah (spoils of war, taken by force) and al-fay' (property gained without battle) are two names for wealth that the Muslims obtain from the property of the disbelievers. A group held that they are one and the same. Others held that they differ: al-ghanimah is what the Muslims take from them by force in battle, while al-fay' is what comes through a peace agreement without fighting. In this verse Allah, mighty and majestic, mentions the ruling on al-ghanimah, saying: ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it and to the Messenger﴾ [[See: al-Tabari 13/545–548; al-Qurtubi 8/1 onward; Ahkam al-Qur'an by Ibn al-'Arabi 2/855 onward; Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas 4/229 onward; al-Kharaj by Abu Yusuf pp. 19–30; al-Kharaj by Yahya ibn Adam pp. 18–45; al-Amwal by Abu 'Ubayd p. 28 onward. These contain a detailed account of the scholars' and exegetes' opinions on the distribution of al-fay' and al-ghanimah.]].

Most exegetes and jurists held that His saying "lillah" (for Allah) is the opening of a statement intended as a blessing, and an ascription of this wealth to Himself to honour it. It does not mean that one share of the spoils belongs to Allah alone, since the whole of this world and the next belong to Allah, mighty and majestic. This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Ata', Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi, who said: "The share of Allah and the share of the Messenger are one." The spoils are divided into five parts: four-fifths go to those who fought for them, and the one-fifth (khums) is for five categories, as Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned: ﴿and to the Messenger, to the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the traveller.﴾

Some said: the one-fifth is divided into six shares, which is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah: one share for Allah, which is spent on the Ka'bah. But the first view is more correct: the one-fifth of the spoils is divided into five shares. One share was for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime, and today it is for the public interests of the Muslims and whatever strengthens Islam. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

al-A'mash narrated from Ibrahim who said: "Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to allocate the Prophet's (ﷺ) share to horses and weapons."

Qatadah said: "It belongs to the caliph after him." Some said: "The share of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is returned to the one-fifth, and the one-fifth goes to four categories."

His saying: ﴿and to the near of kin﴾ means that a share of the one-fifth is for the near of kin, who are the relatives of the Prophet (ﷺ). They differed about who they are. Some said: all of the Quraysh. Others said: those for whom charity is not permitted.

Mujahid and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said: they are the Banu Hashim.

al-Shafi'i said: they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and the Banu 'Abd Shams and the Banu Nawfal have no share of it, even though they are brothers. The evidence for this is what:

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: a trustworthy narrator informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided the share of the near of kin between the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and he gave nothing of it to any of the Banu 'Abd Shams or the Banu Nawfal." [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad 2/112. See also al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi, Bab Ghazwat Khaybar 7/484, and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/126.]]

And Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Mutarrif ibn Mazin informed us, from Ma'mar ibn Rashid, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed me, from his father, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided the share of the near of kin between the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, I came to him, along with 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, and we said: 'O Messenger of Allah, these are our brothers from the Banu Hashim. We do not deny their excellence because of your position, which Allah has given you among them. But what of our brothers from the Banu al-Muttalib? You gave to them and left us out, or you withheld from us, though our kinship and theirs is one.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib are one and the same,' and he interlaced his fingers." [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad 2/111; Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Kharaj wa al-Imarah, Bab fi Bayan Mawadi' Qasm al-Khums 4/220–221; al-Nasa'i in Qasm al-Fay' 7/130–131; Ibn Majah in Kitab al-Jihad, Bab Qismat al-Khums 2/961; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/125–126; al-Tabari in his Tafsir 13/556.]]

The scholars differed over whether the share of the near of kin still applies today. Most of them held that it does, and this is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i. The people of opinion (Ahl al-Ra'y, the Hanafi school) held that it does not apply, and they said: the share of the Messenger of Allah and the share of the near of kin are both returned into the one-fifth, and the one-fifth of the spoils is for three categories: the orphans, the needy and the traveller. Some said: it is given to the poor among them, not to the rich.

The Book and the Sunnah both indicate that it is established. The caliphs after the Messenger (ﷺ) used to give it, and a poor person is not preferred over a rich one, because the Prophet (ﷺ) and the caliphs after him used to give al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, despite the abundance of his wealth. Al-Shafi'i therefore linked it to inheritance, which is due by the name of kinship, except that both the near and the distant relative receive it. He said: the male is preferred over the female, so the man receives two shares and the woman one share.

His saying: ﴿and the orphans﴾, which is the plural of yatim (orphan). The orphan who has a share in the one-fifth is the young Muslim who has no father, provided he is poor. ﴿And the needy﴾ are the people of want and need among the Muslims. ﴿And the traveller﴾ is the traveller far from his wealth. This is the allocation of the one-fifth of the spoils. The four-fifths of the spoils are divided among the warriors who were present at the battle: a horseman among them receives three shares, and a foot soldier one share, based on what:

Abu Salih Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Mu'addhin informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf informed us: Abu Sa'id ibn al-A'rabi informed us: Sa'dan ibn Nasr informed us: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah, from 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) allotted a man and his horse three shares: one share for him and two shares for his horse. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jihad, Bab Sihaam al-Faras 6/67; Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab Kayfiyyat Qismat al-Ghanimah bayn al-Hadirin, no. 1762, 3/1382; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/101.]] This is the view of most scholars. Al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Malik, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq all held it.

Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: a horseman receives two shares, and a foot soldier one share.

Those who are not full combatants, such as slaves, women and children, receive a radkh (a small gift), if they attend the fighting. Property that the Muslims seized, such as land, is divided just like movable property. According to Abu Hanifah, the imam has the choice regarding land: either to divide it among them, or to make it an endowment for the public interests. The apparent meaning of the verse does not distinguish between land and movable property.

Whoever kills a polytheist in battle is entitled to his salab (spoils from the slain enemy) before the division of the spoils, based on what was narrated from Abu Qatadah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of Hunayn: "Whoever kills an enemy for whom he has proof, his salab is his." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi, Bab Qawl Allah Ta'ala "wa Yawm Hunayn idh A'jabatkum Kathratukum" 8/34–35, and he also narrated it in Kitab al-Jihad; Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab Istihqaq Salab al-Qatil, no. 1751, 3/1370; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/105–106.]] The salab is everything on the slain person that is worn or used as a weapon, including the horse he was riding.

The imam may grant (nafl, an extra share) to some of the army from the spoils, in recognition of the greater effort and valour they show in the war. He singles them out from the rest of the army with it, and makes it equal to the shares of the group in the division of the spoils. [[Clarification: nafl means an extra award given beyond the regular share.]]

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliyhi: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Yahya ibn Bukayr informed us: al-Layth informed us, from 'Aqil, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to give an extra share to some of those he sent out on expeditions (sariyyah), for themselves only, apart from the share of the general army. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, Kitab Fard al-Khums, Bab wa min al-Dalil 'ala an al-Khums li-Nawa'ib al-Muslimin 6/237; Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab al-Anfal, no. 1750, 3/1369; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/112.]]

It was narrated from Habib ibn Maslamah al-Fihri, who said: "I witnessed the Prophet (ﷺ) give a quarter as an extra share at the beginning of the expedition, and a third on the return." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Jihad, Bab fiman Qala: al-Khums Qabl al-Nafl 4/57; and al-Tirmidhi, Kitab al-Siyar, Bab fi al-Nafl 5/176, from the hadith of 'Ubadah, who said it is hasan (sound); he said: "There is also a report on this from Ibn 'Abbas, Habib ibn Maslamah, Ma'n ibn Yazid, Ibn 'Umar and Salamah ibn al-Akwa'." Also narrated by Ibn Majah, no. 2852, 2/951–952, who said in al-Zawa'id: its isnad is hasan; Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. 1672, p. 403 of Mawarid al-Zam'an. Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in al-Sunan 2/262, and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 4/160.]]

The scholars differed over where the extra share is to be taken from. Some said: from the one-fifth of the one-fifth, the share of the Prophet (ﷺ). This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and al-Shafi'i also said it. This is the meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "I have no share of what Allah has given you as fay' except the one-fifth, and that one-fifth is returned to you." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Jihad, Bab al-Imam Yastathir bi-Shay' min al-Fay' li-Nafsihi, with a different wording, 4/62; al-Nasa'i in al-Fay' 7/131–132; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 4/128 and 5/316; and cited in al-Durr al-Manthur 4/67 as narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

Others said: it is taken from the four-fifths after the one-fifth is separated, like the shares of the fighters. This is the view of Ahmad and Ishaq.

Some held that the extra share is taken from the top of the spoils before the one-fifth, like the salab for the slayer.

As for al-fay', which is what the Muslims obtain from the property of the disbelievers without the pressing of horses or camels (without battle), such as when they make a peace agreement with them in return for property they pay, and the jizyah (poll tax) money, and what is taken from their property when they enter the abode of Islam for trade, or when one of them dies in the abode of Islam with no heir, all of this is fay'.

The property of the fay' was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Indeed Allah specially favoured the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with something in this fay' that He gave to no one else," [[This is found in many authentic, lengthy reports, which al-Suyuti cited in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/101–103.]] then he recited: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿...is powerful.﴾ [al-Hashr 59:6]. This was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who would spend on his household and dependents the full year's maintenance from this property, and then he would take what remained and place it where the property of Allah, mighty and majestic, is placed.

The sources differed about how the fay' (spoils gained without battle) was to be spent after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some scholars said: it belongs to the leaders (al-A'immah) after him. Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) had two opinions on this. The first: it goes to the fighters (al-muqatilah) whose names are registered in the register of jihad (diwan al-jihad), because they stand in the place of the Prophet (ﷺ) in striking terror into the enemy. The second: it is for the public interests of the Muslims. It begins with the fighters, who are given what suffices them from it, and then goes to the most important of the interests, in order of their importance.

The scholars also differed concerning the division of the fay' into fifths (takhmis al-fay'). Al-Shafi'i held that one-fifth of it is set aside (yukhammas khumusuh) for the people of the ghanimah (spoils of war), divided into five shares, and that the remaining four-fifths go to the fighters and to the public interests.

Most scholars held that the fay' is not divided into fifths. Rather, the whole of it has a single line of expenditure, and all Muslims have a right in it:

Abu Sa'id 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed us: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Udhafiri informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Dabari informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadthan, that he heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) say: "There is no Muslim on the face of the earth but that he has a right in this fay', except what your right hands possess."[[Narrated by al-Shafi'i (2/127), and 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (no. 20039), and Abu 'Ubayd in al-Amwal (p. 243, Qatar edition), and Yahya ibn Adam in al-Kharaj (p. 42), and al-Bayhaqi (6/347), and in its chain is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-'Umari, who is weak from the seventh tier (Taqrib). See also: Irwa' al-Ghalil of al-Albani (5/83), Kanz al-'Ummal (4/525).]]

And Abu Sa'id al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed us: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Udhafiri informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Dabari informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadthan, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) recited: "The alms are only for the poor and the needy..." until he reached "...All-Knowing, All-Wise" (At-Tawbah 9:60). He said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: "And know that whatever you gain of spoils, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger..." until he reached "...and the wayfarer" (Al-Anfal 8:41). Then he said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: "What Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns..." until he reached "...for the poor emigrants who were driven out..." (Al-Hashr 59:7–9). Then he said: "This has covered all the Muslims in general. If I live, the shepherd in Sarw Himyar will certainly receive his share of it, without his brow having to sweat for it."[[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (no. 20040), and Abu 'Ubayd in similar wording in al-Amwal (pp. 25 and 244). Al-Bukhari narrated it at length, in similar wording, in the chapters on the obligation of the khums, on the campaigns (al-Maghazi) and on tafsir, and Muslim in the chapter on jihad. See also: al-Bayhaqi (6/352), Sharh al-Sunnah (11/131–134).]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you have believed in Allah﴾. It has been said that He meant: "Know that whatever you gain of spoils, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger," and He commands regarding it what He wills, so accept it, if you have believed in Allah. ﴿And what We sent down upon Our servant﴾, that is: if you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down upon Our servant, meaning His saying: "They ask you about the spoils (al-anfal)." ﴿On the Day of Criterion﴾, meaning the Day of Badr, when Allah distinguished between truth and falsehood, ﴿the day the two hosts met﴾, the party of Allah and the party of Satan. It was a Friday, on the seventeenth of Ramadan. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, over granting you victory despite your small number and their large number.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 39–41 (part 1 of 2):

﴿And fight them until there is no more fitnah,﴾ that is, shirk (associating others with God). Al-Rabi' said: "Until no believer is tempted away from his religion." ﴿And religion is entirely for Allah,﴾ that is, religion becomes purely for Allah, with no shirk in it. ﴿But if they cease﴾ from disbelief, ﴿then indeed Allah is Seeing of what they do.﴾ Ya'qub read "ta'malun" (with a ta' at the beginning, addressing them), while the others read it with a ya' ("ya'malun").

﴿But if they turn away﴾ from faith and return to fighting its people, ﴿then know that Allah is your Protector (mawlakum),﴾ your Helper and Supporter, ﴿an excellent Protector and an excellent Helper.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of any spoils (ghanimtum min shay'),﴾ ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it,﴾ and so on. Al-ghanimah (spoils of war, taken by force) and al-fay' (property gained without battle) are two names for wealth that the Muslims obtain from the property of the disbelievers. A group held that they are one and the same. Others held that they differ: al-ghanimah is what the Muslims take from them by force in battle, while al-fay' is what comes through a peace agreement without fighting. In this verse Allah, mighty and majestic, mentions the ruling on al-ghanimah, saying: ﴿then to Allah belongs one-fifth of it and to the Messenger﴾ [[See: al-Tabari 13/545–548; al-Qurtubi 8/1 onward; Ahkam al-Qur'an by Ibn al-'Arabi 2/855 onward; Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas 4/229 onward; al-Kharaj by Abu Yusuf pp. 19–30; al-Kharaj by Yahya ibn Adam pp. 18–45; al-Amwal by Abu 'Ubayd p. 28 onward. These contain a detailed account of the scholars' and exegetes' opinions on the distribution of al-fay' and al-ghanimah.]].

Most exegetes and jurists held that His saying "lillah" (for Allah) is the opening of a statement intended as a blessing, and an ascription of this wealth to Himself to honour it. It does not mean that one share of the spoils belongs to Allah alone, since the whole of this world and the next belong to Allah, mighty and majestic. This is the view of al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Ata', Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi, who said: "The share of Allah and the share of the Messenger are one." The spoils are divided into five parts: four-fifths go to those who fought for them, and the one-fifth (khums) is for five categories, as Allah, mighty and majestic, mentioned: ﴿and to the Messenger, to the near of kin, the orphans, the needy, and the traveller.﴾

Some said: the one-fifth is divided into six shares, which is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah: one share for Allah, which is spent on the Ka'bah. But the first view is more correct: the one-fifth of the spoils is divided into five shares. One share was for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime, and today it is for the public interests of the Muslims and whatever strengthens Islam. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him.

al-A'mash narrated from Ibrahim who said: "Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to allocate the Prophet's (ﷺ) share to horses and weapons."

Qatadah said: "It belongs to the caliph after him." Some said: "The share of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is returned to the one-fifth, and the one-fifth goes to four categories."

His saying: ﴿and to the near of kin﴾ means that a share of the one-fifth is for the near of kin, who are the relatives of the Prophet (ﷺ). They differed about who they are. Some said: all of the Quraysh. Others said: those for whom charity is not permitted.

Mujahid and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said: they are the Banu Hashim.

al-Shafi'i said: they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and the Banu 'Abd Shams and the Banu Nawfal have no share of it, even though they are brothers. The evidence for this is what:

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: a trustworthy narrator informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided the share of the near of kin between the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and he gave nothing of it to any of the Banu 'Abd Shams or the Banu Nawfal." [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad 2/112. See also al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi, Bab Ghazwat Khaybar 7/484, and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/126.]]

And Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Mutarrif ibn Mazin informed us, from Ma'mar ibn Rashid, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed me, from his father, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided the share of the near of kin between the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, I came to him, along with 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, and we said: 'O Messenger of Allah, these are our brothers from the Banu Hashim. We do not deny their excellence because of your position, which Allah has given you among them. But what of our brothers from the Banu al-Muttalib? You gave to them and left us out, or you withheld from us, though our kinship and theirs is one.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib are one and the same,' and he interlaced his fingers." [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad 2/111; Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Kharaj wa al-Imarah, Bab fi Bayan Mawadi' Qasm al-Khums 4/220–221; al-Nasa'i in Qasm al-Fay' 7/130–131; Ibn Majah in Kitab al-Jihad, Bab Qismat al-Khums 2/961; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/125–126; al-Tabari in his Tafsir 13/556.]]

The scholars differed over whether the share of the near of kin still applies today. Most of them held that it does, and this is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i. The people of opinion (Ahl al-Ra'y, the Hanafi school) held that it does not apply, and they said: the share of the Messenger of Allah and the share of the near of kin are both returned into the one-fifth, and the one-fifth of the spoils is for three categories: the orphans, the needy and the traveller. Some said: it is given to the poor among them, not to the rich.

The Book and the Sunnah both indicate that it is established. The caliphs after the Messenger (ﷺ) used to give it, and a poor person is not preferred over a rich one, because the Prophet (ﷺ) and the caliphs after him used to give al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, despite the abundance of his wealth. Al-Shafi'i therefore linked it to inheritance, which is due by the name of kinship, except that both the near and the distant relative receive it. He said: the male is preferred over the female, so the man receives two shares and the woman one share.

His saying: ﴿and the orphans﴾, which is the plural of yatim (orphan). The orphan who has a share in the one-fifth is the young Muslim who has no father, provided he is poor. ﴿And the needy﴾ are the people of want and need among the Muslims. ﴿And the traveller﴾ is the traveller far from his wealth. This is the allocation of the one-fifth of the spoils. The four-fifths of the spoils are divided among the warriors who were present at the battle: a horseman among them receives three shares, and a foot soldier one share, based on what:

Abu Salih Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Mu'addhin informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf informed us: Abu Sa'id ibn al-A'rabi informed us: Sa'dan ibn Nasr informed us: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah, from 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) allotted a man and his horse three shares: one share for him and two shares for his horse. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jihad, Bab Sihaam al-Faras 6/67; Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab Kayfiyyat Qismat al-Ghanimah bayn al-Hadirin, no. 1762, 3/1382; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/101.]] This is the view of most scholars. Al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Malik, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq all held it.

Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: a horseman receives two shares, and a foot soldier one share.

Those who are not full combatants, such as slaves, women and children, receive a radkh (a small gift), if they attend the fighting. Property that the Muslims seized, such as land, is divided just like movable property. According to Abu Hanifah, the imam has the choice regarding land: either to divide it among them, or to make it an endowment for the public interests. The apparent meaning of the verse does not distinguish between land and movable property.

Whoever kills a polytheist in battle is entitled to his salab (spoils from the slain enemy) before the division of the spoils, based on what was narrated from Abu Qatadah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of Hunayn: "Whoever kills an enemy for whom he has proof, his salab is his." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi, Bab Qawl Allah Ta'ala "wa Yawm Hunayn idh A'jabatkum Kathratukum" 8/34–35, and he also narrated it in Kitab al-Jihad; Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab Istihqaq Salab al-Qatil, no. 1751, 3/1370; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/105–106.]] The salab is everything on the slain person that is worn or used as a weapon, including the horse he was riding.

The imam may grant (nafl, an extra share) to some of the army from the spoils, in recognition of the greater effort and valour they show in the war. He singles them out from the rest of the army with it, and makes it equal to the shares of the group in the division of the spoils. [[Clarification: nafl means an extra award given beyond the regular share.]]

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliyhi: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Yahya ibn Bukayr informed us: al-Layth informed us, from 'Aqil, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to give an extra share to some of those he sent out on expeditions (sariyyah), for themselves only, apart from the share of the general army. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, Kitab Fard al-Khums, Bab wa min al-Dalil 'ala an al-Khums li-Nawa'ib al-Muslimin 6/237; Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab al-Anfal, no. 1750, 3/1369; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/112.]]

It was narrated from Habib ibn Maslamah al-Fihri, who said: "I witnessed the Prophet (ﷺ) give a quarter as an extra share at the beginning of the expedition, and a third on the return." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Jihad, Bab fiman Qala: al-Khums Qabl al-Nafl 4/57; and al-Tirmidhi, Kitab al-Siyar, Bab fi al-Nafl 5/176, from the hadith of 'Ubadah, who said it is hasan (sound); he said: "There is also a report on this from Ibn 'Abbas, Habib ibn Maslamah, Ma'n ibn Yazid, Ibn 'Umar and Salamah ibn al-Akwa'." Also narrated by Ibn Majah, no. 2852, 2/951–952, who said in al-Zawa'id: its isnad is hasan; Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. 1672, p. 403 of Mawarid al-Zam'an. Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in al-Sunan 2/262, and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 4/160.]]

The scholars differed over where the extra share is to be taken from. Some said: from the one-fifth of the one-fifth, the share of the Prophet (ﷺ). This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and al-Shafi'i also said it. This is the meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "I have no share of what Allah has given you as fay' except the one-fifth, and that one-fifth is returned to you." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Jihad, Bab al-Imam Yastathir bi-Shay' min al-Fay' li-Nafsihi, with a different wording, 4/62; al-Nasa'i in al-Fay' 7/131–132; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 4/128 and 5/316; and cited in al-Durr al-Manthur 4/67 as narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

Others said: it is taken from the four-fifths after the one-fifth is separated, like the shares of the fighters. This is the view of Ahmad and Ishaq.

Some held that the extra share is taken from the top of the spoils before the one-fifth, like the salab for the slayer.

As for al-fay', which is what the Muslims obtain from the property of the disbelievers without the pressing of horses or camels (without battle), such as when they make a peace agreement with them in return for property they pay, and the jizyah (poll tax) money, and what is taken from their property when they enter the abode of Islam for trade, or when one of them dies in the abode of Islam with no heir, all of this is fay'.

The property of the fay' was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Indeed Allah specially favoured the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with something in this fay' that He gave to no one else," [[This is found in many authentic, lengthy reports, which al-Suyuti cited in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/101–103.]] then he recited: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿...is powerful.﴾ [al-Hashr 59:6]. This was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who would spend on his household and dependents the full year's maintenance from this property, and then he would take what remained and place it where the property of Allah, mighty and majestic, is placed.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) had two opinions on this.
