Mujahid and 'Ali ibn al-Husayn said: they are the Banu Hashim.

al-Shafi'i said: they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and the Banu 'Abd Shams and the Banu Nawfal have no share of it, even though they are brothers. The evidence for this is what:

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: a trustworthy narrator informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Ibn al-Musayyab, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided the share of the near of kin between the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and he gave nothing of it to any of the Banu 'Abd Shams or the Banu Nawfal." [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad 2/112. See also al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi, Bab Ghazwat Khaybar 7/484, and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/126.]]

And Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Mutarrif ibn Mazin informed us, from Ma'mar ibn Rashid, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im informed me, from his father, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided the share of the near of kin between the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, I came to him, along with 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, and we said: 'O Messenger of Allah, these are our brothers from the Banu Hashim. We do not deny their excellence because of your position, which Allah has given you among them. But what of our brothers from the Banu al-Muttalib? You gave to them and left us out, or you withheld from us, though our kinship and theirs is one.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'The Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib are one and the same,' and he interlaced his fingers." [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad 2/111; Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Kharaj wa al-Imarah, Bab fi Bayan Mawadi' Qasm al-Khums 4/220–221; al-Nasa'i in Qasm al-Fay' 7/130–131; Ibn Majah in Kitab al-Jihad, Bab Qismat al-Khums 2/961; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/125–126; al-Tabari in his Tafsir 13/556.]]

The scholars differed over whether the share of the near of kin still applies today. Most of them held that it does, and this is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i. The people of opinion (Ahl al-Ra'y, the Hanafi school) held that it does not apply, and they said: the share of the Messenger of Allah and the share of the near of kin are both returned into the one-fifth, and the one-fifth of the spoils is for three categories: the orphans, the needy and the traveller. Some said: it is given to the poor among them, not to the rich.

The Book and the Sunnah both indicate that it is established. The caliphs after the Messenger (ﷺ) used to give it, and a poor person is not preferred over a rich one, because the Prophet (ﷺ) and the caliphs after him used to give al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, despite the abundance of his wealth. Al-Shafi'i therefore linked it to inheritance, which is due by the name of kinship, except that both the near and the distant relative receive it. He said: the male is preferred over the female, so the man receives two shares and the woman one share.

His saying: ﴿and the orphans﴾, which is the plural of yatim (orphan). The orphan who has a share in the one-fifth is the young Muslim who has no father, provided he is poor. ﴿And the needy﴾ are the people of want and need among the Muslims. ﴿And the traveller﴾ is the traveller far from his wealth. This is the allocation of the one-fifth of the spoils. The four-fifths of the spoils are divided among the warriors who were present at the battle: a horseman among them receives three shares, and a foot soldier one share, based on what:

Abu Salih Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Mu'addhin informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf informed us: Abu Sa'id ibn al-A'rabi informed us: Sa'dan ibn Nasr informed us: Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah, from 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) allotted a man and his horse three shares: one share for him and two shares for his horse. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Jihad, Bab Sihaam al-Faras 6/67; Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab Kayfiyyat Qismat al-Ghanimah bayn al-Hadirin, no. 1762, 3/1382; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/101.]] This is the view of most scholars. Al-Thawri, al-Awza'i, Malik, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq all held it.

Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: a horseman receives two shares, and a foot soldier one share.

Those who are not full combatants, such as slaves, women and children, receive a radkh (a small gift), if they attend the fighting. Property that the Muslims seized, such as land, is divided just like movable property. According to Abu Hanifah, the imam has the choice regarding land: either to divide it among them, or to make it an endowment for the public interests. The apparent meaning of the verse does not distinguish between land and movable property.

Whoever kills a polytheist in battle is entitled to his salab (spoils from the slain enemy) before the division of the spoils, based on what was narrated from Abu Qatadah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of Hunayn: "Whoever kills an enemy for whom he has proof, his salab is his." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Maghazi, Bab Qawl Allah Ta'ala "wa Yawm Hunayn idh A'jabatkum Kathratukum" 8/34–35, and he also narrated it in Kitab al-Jihad; Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab Istihqaq Salab al-Qatil, no. 1751, 3/1370; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/105–106.]] The salab is everything on the slain person that is worn or used as a weapon, including the horse he was riding.

The imam may grant (nafl, an extra share) to some of the army from the spoils, in recognition of the greater effort and valour they show in the war. He singles them out from the rest of the army with it, and makes it equal to the shares of the group in the division of the spoils. [[Clarification: nafl means an extra award given beyond the regular share.]]

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliyhi: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Yahya ibn Bukayr informed us: al-Layth informed us, from 'Aqil, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to give an extra share to some of those he sent out on expeditions (sariyyah), for themselves only, apart from the share of the general army. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, Kitab Fard al-Khums, Bab wa min al-Dalil 'ala an al-Khums li-Nawa'ib al-Muslimin 6/237; Muslim, Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab al-Anfal, no. 1750, 3/1369; al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah 11/112.]]

It was narrated from Habib ibn Maslamah al-Fihri, who said: "I witnessed the Prophet (ﷺ) give a quarter as an extra share at the beginning of the expedition, and a third on the return." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Jihad, Bab fiman Qala: al-Khums Qabl al-Nafl 4/57; and al-Tirmidhi, Kitab al-Siyar, Bab fi al-Nafl 5/176, from the hadith of 'Ubadah, who said it is hasan (sound); he said: "There is also a report on this from Ibn 'Abbas, Habib ibn Maslamah, Ma'n ibn Yazid, Ibn 'Umar and Salamah ibn al-Akwa'." Also narrated by Ibn Majah, no. 2852, 2/951–952, who said in al-Zawa'id: its isnad is hasan; Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. 1672, p. 403 of Mawarid al-Zam'an. Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it in al-Sunan 2/262, and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 4/160.]]

The scholars differed over where the extra share is to be taken from. Some said: from the one-fifth of the one-fifth, the share of the Prophet (ﷺ). This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and al-Shafi'i also said it. This is the meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "I have no share of what Allah has given you as fay' except the one-fifth, and that one-fifth is returned to you." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud, Kitab al-Jihad, Bab al-Imam Yastathir bi-Shay' min al-Fay' li-Nafsihi, with a different wording, 4/62; al-Nasa'i in al-Fay' 7/131–132; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 4/128 and 5/316; and cited in al-Durr al-Manthur 4/67 as narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

Others said: it is taken from the four-fifths after the one-fifth is separated, like the shares of the fighters. This is the view of Ahmad and Ishaq.

Some held that the extra share is taken from the top of the spoils before the one-fifth, like the salab for the slayer.

As for al-fay', which is what the Muslims obtain from the property of the disbelievers without the pressing of horses or camels (without battle), such as when they make a peace agreement with them in return for property they pay, and the jizyah (poll tax) money, and what is taken from their property when they enter the abode of Islam for trade, or when one of them dies in the abode of Islam with no heir, all of this is fay'.

The property of the fay' was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Indeed Allah specially favoured the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with something in this fay' that He gave to no one else," [[This is found in many authentic, lengthy reports, which al-Suyuti cited in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/101–103.]] then he recited: ﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿...is powerful.﴾ [al-Hashr 59:6]. This was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who would spend on his household and dependents the full year's maintenance from this property, and then he would take what remained and place it where the property of Allah, mighty and majestic, is placed.

The sources differed about how the fay' (spoils gained without battle) was to be spent after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some scholars said: it belongs to the leaders (al-A'immah) after him. Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) had two opinions on this. The first: it goes to the fighters (al-muqatilah) whose names are registered in the register of jihad (diwan al-jihad), because they stand in the place of the Prophet (ﷺ) in striking terror into the enemy. The second: it is for the public interests of the Muslims. It begins with the fighters, who are given what suffices them from it, and then goes to the most important of the interests, in order of their importance.

The scholars also differed concerning the division of the fay' into fifths (takhmis al-fay'). Al-Shafi'i held that one-fifth of it is set aside (yukhammas khumusuh) for the people of the ghanimah (spoils of war), divided into five shares, and that the remaining four-fifths go to the fighters and to the public interests.

Most scholars held that the fay' is not divided into fifths. Rather, the whole of it has a single line of expenditure, and all Muslims have a right in it:

Abu Sa'id 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed us: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Udhafiri informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Dabari informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadthan, that he heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) say: "There is no Muslim on the face of the earth but that he has a right in this fay', except what your right hands possess."[[Narrated by al-Shafi'i (2/127), and 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (no. 20039), and Abu 'Ubayd in al-Amwal (p. 243, Qatar edition), and Yahya ibn Adam in al-Kharaj (p. 42), and al-Bayhaqi (6/347), and in its chain is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-'Umari, who is weak from the seventh tier (Taqrib). See also: Irwa' al-Ghalil of al-Albani (5/83), Kanz al-'Ummal (4/525).]]

And Abu Sa'id al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzaz informed us: Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-'Udhafiri informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Dabari informed us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadthan, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) recited: "The alms are only for the poor and the needy..." until he reached "...All-Knowing, All-Wise" (At-Tawbah 9:60). He said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: "And know that whatever you gain of spoils, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger..." until he reached "...and the wayfarer" (Al-Anfal 8:41). Then he said: "This is for these people." Then he recited: "What Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns..." until he reached "...for the poor emigrants who were driven out..." (Al-Hashr 59:7–9). Then he said: "This has covered all the Muslims in general. If I live, the shepherd in Sarw Himyar will certainly receive his share of it, without his brow having to sweat for it."[[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (no. 20040), and Abu 'Ubayd in similar wording in al-Amwal (pp. 25 and 244). Al-Bukhari narrated it at length, in similar wording, in the chapters on the obligation of the khums, on the campaigns (al-Maghazi) and on tafsir, and Muslim in the chapter on jihad. See also: al-Bayhaqi (6/352), Sharh al-Sunnah (11/131–134).]]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you have believed in Allah﴾. It has been said that He meant: "Know that whatever you gain of spoils, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger," and He commands regarding it what He wills, so accept it, if you have believed in Allah. ﴿And what We sent down upon Our servant﴾, that is: if you have believed in Allah and in what We sent down upon Our servant, meaning His saying: "They ask you about the spoils (al-anfal)." ﴿On the Day of Criterion﴾, meaning the Day of Badr, when Allah distinguished between truth and falsehood, ﴿the day the two hosts met﴾, the party of Allah and the party of Satan. It was a Friday, on the seventeenth of Ramadan. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent﴾, over granting you victory despite your small number and their large number.

﴿When you were﴾, that is, when you were encamped, O company of Muslims, ﴿on the nearer bank﴾, that is, on the edge of the nearer valley to Madinah. *al-Dunya* is the feminine of *al-adna* (nearer). ﴿And they were﴾, meaning your enemy among the polytheists, ﴿on the farther bank﴾,

on the edge of the farther valley from Madinah. *al-Quswa* is the feminine of *al-aqsa* (farthest).

Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read *"bil-'idwati"* with a kasra on the 'ayn in both places. The rest read it with a damma. Both are dialectal variants, like *al-kiswah* and *al-kuswah*, and *al-rishwah* and *al-rushwah*.

﴿And the caravan﴾, meaning the trade caravan, intending Abu Sufyan and his companions, ﴿was lower than you﴾, that is, in a place lower than you, extending to the seashore, three miles from Badr. ﴿Even if you had made an appointment together, you would have differed about the appointment.﴾ This is because the Muslims went out to seize the caravan, and the unbelievers went out to protect it. They met without any appointment. Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Even if you had made an appointment together, you would have differed about the appointment﴾, because of your small number and your enemy's large number. ﴿But﴾ God gathered you without an appointment ﴿so that God might accomplish a matter that was to be done﴾, namely the victory of His friends, the exaltation of His religion, and the destruction of His enemies. ﴿So that whoever would perish might perish upon clear evidence﴾, that is, so that whoever would die might die after a clear sign he had seen, a lesson he had witnessed, and a proof established against him.

﴿And whoever would live might live upon clear evidence﴾, and whoever lives might live upon clear evidence, in accordance with His promise: "And We would never punish until We sent a messenger" (al-Isra: 15). Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: its meaning is that whoever disbelieves after a proof has been established against him disbelieves, and whoever believes believes on the same basis. So destruction is disbelief, and life is faith.

Qatadah said: so that whoever goes astray after clear evidence may go astray, and whoever is guided may be guided upon clear evidence.

The people of the Hijaz, Abu Bakr and Ya'qub read *"hayiya"* with two yas, like *"khashiya"*. The others read it with one yа shaddah, because it is written with one ya.

﴿And indeed God is All-Hearing﴾ of your supplication, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of your intentions.

The Prophet's words: ﴿When Allah showed them to you﴾ means He shows you, O Muhammad, the polytheists, ﴿in your dream﴾, that is, in your sleep. Al-Hasan said: "in your dream" means "in your eye," because the eye is the place of sleep. ﴿A few; and if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart﴾, meaning you would have become cowardly, ﴿and you would have disputed about the matter﴾, that is, you would have differed about the matter of holding back or advancing. ﴿But Allah saved [you]﴾, that is, He saved you from opposition and failure. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾. Ibn Abbas said: He knows what is in your breasts of love for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes﴾. Muqatil said: This was because the Prophet (ﷺ) saw in a dream that the enemy was few, before meeting the enemy, and he informed his Companions of what he had seen. When they met at Badr, Allah made the polytheists appear few in the eyes of the believers.

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They appeared so few in our eyes that I said to a man beside me, 'Do you think they are seventy?' He said, 'I think they are a hundred.' Then we captured a man and asked him, 'How many were you?' He said, 'A thousand.'"

﴿And He made you appear few﴾, O company of believers, ﴿in their eyes﴾. Al-Suddi said: Some of the polytheists said, "The caravan has turned back, so return." Abu Jahl said, "Now, when Muhammad and his Companions have come out against you? Do not return until you have wiped them out. Muhammad and his Companions are only people who eat camel meat; so do not kill them, but bind them with ropes." (He said this out of the power that was in himself.) Al-Kalbi said: Some of them belittled others so that they would be bold in fighting. So Allah made the polytheists appear few in the eyes of the believers, so that they would not lose heart, and made the believers appear few in the eyes of the polytheists, so that they would not flee.

﴿That Allah might accomplish a matter﴾ of exalting Islam, honoring its people, and humbling polytheism and its people.

﴿Which was to be done﴾, meaning existing. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾.

The Prophet's words: ﴿When Allah showed them to you﴾ means He shows you, O Muhammad, the polytheists, ﴿in your dream﴾, that is, in your sleep. Al-Hasan said: "in your dream" means "in your eye," because the eye is the place of sleep. ﴿A few; and if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost heart﴾, meaning you would have become cowardly, ﴿and you would have disputed about the matter﴾, that is, you would have differed about the matter of holding back or advancing. ﴿But Allah saved [you]﴾, that is, He saved you from opposition and failure. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾. Ibn Abbas said: He knows what is in your breasts of love for Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes﴾. Muqatil said: This was because the Prophet (ﷺ) saw in a dream that the enemy was few, before meeting the enemy, and he informed his Companions of what he had seen. When they met at Badr, Allah made the polytheists appear few in the eyes of the believers.

Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "They appeared so few in our eyes that I said to a man beside me, 'Do you think they are seventy?' He said, 'I think they are a hundred.' Then we captured a man and asked him, 'How many were you?' He said, 'A thousand.'"

﴿And He made you appear few﴾, O company of believers, ﴿in their eyes﴾. Al-Suddi said: Some of the polytheists said, "The caravan has turned back, so return." Abu Jahl said, "Now, when Muhammad and his Companions have come out against you? Do not return until you have wiped them out. Muhammad and his Companions are only people who eat camel meat; so do not kill them, but bind them with ropes." (He said this out of the power that was in himself.) Al-Kalbi said: Some of them belittled others so that they would be bold in fighting. So Allah made the polytheists appear few in the eyes of the believers, so that they would not lose heart, and made the believers appear few in the eyes of the polytheists, so that they would not flee.

﴿That Allah might accomplish a matter﴾ of exalting Islam, honoring its people, and humbling polytheism and its people.

﴿Which was to be done﴾, meaning existing. ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 8, verses 45–46:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company [of disbelievers]﴾, i.e., a disbelieving group, ﴿then stand firm﴾ for fighting them, ﴿and remember Allah often﴾, i.e., supplicate to Allah for victory and triumph over them, ﴿that you may be successful﴾, i.e., be hopeful of success.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger and do not dispute, lest you lose courage﴾, i.e., become cowardly and weak, ﴿and your strength [rih] would depart﴾. Mujahid said: "Your support." Al-Suddi said: "Your boldness and your good fortune." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "Your vigour." Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "Your power." Al-Akhfash said: "Your dynasty." Here "rih" (wind) is a metaphor for the execution of a command and its proceeding according to what is intended. The Arabs say: "The wind of so-and-so has blown," when his affair turns out according to what he desires.

Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: "It is the wind of victory. Victory never happened except by a wind that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends, striking the faces of the enemy."

From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I have been given victory by the east wind (al-saba), and 'Ad were destroyed by the west wind (al-dabur)."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Istisqa', chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) "I was given victory by the saba": 2/520, and in Bad' al-Khalq and al-Anbiya'; and Muslim in al-Istisqa', chapter on the saba and dabur winds, no. (900): 2/617; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/387.]]

And on the authority of al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin, who said: "I witnessed [battle] with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he did not fight at the beginning of the day, he would wait until the sun declined, the winds blew, and victory descended."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on what time it is preferable to meet [the enemy]: 4/7; and al-Tirmidhi in al-Siyar, chapter on what has come concerning the hour in which fighting is preferred: 5/238, and he said: "A hasan sahih hadith." And al-Hakim: 2/116, and he authenticated it on the condition of Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/444–445; and al-Mundhiri in Mukhtasar al-Sunan attributed it to al-Nasa'i.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And be patient; indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, [who said:] Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aimi informed us, [who said:] Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us, [who said:] Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, [who said:] Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us, [who said:] Mu'awiyah ibn Amr related to us, [who said:] Abu Ishaq related to us, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Salim Abi al-Nadr, client of Umar ibn Ubayd Allah, and he was his scribe, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa wrote to him, and I read it: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on some of the days on which he met the enemy, waited until the sun declined. Then he stood among the people and said: "O people, do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. But when you meet them, be patient, and know that Paradise is under the shade of the swords." Then he said: "O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Mover of the clouds, and Defeater of the confederates, defeat them and grant us victory over them."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on the Prophet (ﷺ) when he did not fight at the beginning of the day...: 6/130; and Muslim in al-Jihad and al-Siyar, chapter on the disliking of wishing to meet the enemy (1742): 3/1362; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/38–39.]]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 8, verses 45–46:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you encounter a company [of disbelievers]﴾, i.e., a disbelieving group, ﴿then stand firm﴾ for fighting them, ﴿and remember Allah often﴾, i.e., supplicate to Allah for victory and triumph over them, ﴿that you may be successful﴾, i.e., be hopeful of success.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And obey Allah and His Messenger and do not dispute, lest you lose courage﴾, i.e., become cowardly and weak, ﴿and your strength [rih] would depart﴾. Mujahid said: "Your support." Al-Suddi said: "Your boldness and your good fortune." Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "Your vigour." Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "Your power." Al-Akhfash said: "Your dynasty." The Arabs say: "The wind of so-and-so has blown," when his affair turns out according to what he desires.

Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: "It is the wind of victory. Victory never happened except by a wind that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends, striking the faces of the enemy."

From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I have been given victory by the east wind (al-saba), and 'Ad were destroyed by the west wind (al-dabur)."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Istisqa', chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) "I was given victory by the saba": 2/520, and in Bad' al-Khalq and al-Anbiya'; and Muslim in al-Istisqa', chapter on the saba and dabur winds, no. (900): 2/617; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/387.]]

And on the authority of al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin, who said: "I witnessed [battle] with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When he did not fight at the beginning of the day, he would wait until the sun declined, the winds blew, and victory descended."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on what time it is preferable to meet [the enemy]: 4/7; and al-Tirmidhi in al-Siyar, chapter on what has come concerning the hour in which fighting is preferred: 5/238, and he said: "A hasan sahih hadith." And al-Hakim: 2/116, and he authenticated it on the condition of Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/444–445; and al-Mundhiri in Mukhtasar al-Sunan attributed it to al-Nasa'i.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And be patient; indeed, Allah is with the patient﴾.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, [who said:] Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aimi informed us, [who said:] Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us, [who said:] Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, [who said:] Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us, [who said:] Mu'awiyah ibn Amr related to us, [who said:] Abu Ishaq related to us, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Salim Abi al-Nadr, client of Umar ibn Ubayd Allah, and he was his scribe, who said: Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa wrote to him, and I read it: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on some of the days on which he met the enemy, waited until the sun declined. Then he stood among the people and said: "O people, do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for well-being. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 47–48:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who went forth from their homes insolently (batar)﴾ meaning boastfully and vainly, ﴿and to be seen by people (ri'a' al-nas)﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: al-batar is transgression in blessing and neglecting its thanks, and al-riya' is displaying what is good so as to be seen, while concealing what is ugly. ﴿And they bar from the way of Allah, and Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾. It was revealed concerning the polytheists when they came toward Badr with arrogance and pride. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, these are Quraysh, who have come with their vanity and their pride, contending with You and denying Your Messenger. O Allah, grant us the victory You promised me."

They said: When Abu Sufyan saw that he had secured his caravan, he sent to Quraysh: "You only set out to protect your caravan, and Allah has saved it, so return." But Abu Jahl said: "By Allah, we will not return until we reach Badr." Badr was a seasonal gathering of the Arabs, where a market was held for them every year. We would stay there three days, slaughter camels, feed people, serve wine, and singing-girls (qiyan) would play for us, and the Arabs would hear of us and continue to fear us forever. But they arrived there and were given the cups of death instead of wine, and mourning women wailed over them instead of singing-girls. Thus Allah forbade His believing servants from being like them, and commanded them to sincerity of intention and seeking reward in supporting His religion and aiding His Prophet (ﷺ). [[See above, in the commentary on verse (7) of the surah, and the narrations the author cited there.]]

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Satan made their deeds seem fair to them﴾. His adornment was that when Quraysh gathered to march, they recalled the war between them and the Banu Bakr, which nearly deterred them. Then Iblis came in a host of devils, with his banner, and appeared to them in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum, ﴿and said﴾ to them, ﴿"No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector"﴾, meaning, a defender for you against Kinanah. ﴿Then when the two hosts came in sight of each other﴾, meaning when the two groups met, Iblis saw the angels descending from the sky, and he knew that he had no power against them, ﴿so he turned back on his heels﴾. Al-Dahhak said: he turned and fled. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: he retreated backwards on his back, fleeing. Al-Kalbi said: When they met, Iblis was in the ranks of the polytheists in the form of Suraqah, holding the hand of al-Harith ibn Hisham. When he turned back on his heels, al-Harith said to him: "Are you fleeing without fighting?" He began to hold him, but he pushed him in the chest and departed, and the people were routed. When they returned to Makkah, they said: "Suraqah routed the people." This reached Suraqah, and he said: "It has reached me that you say I routed the people. By Allah, I was not aware of your march until the news of your defeat reached me!" They said: "Did you not come to us on such and such a day?" He swore to them (that he had not). When they embraced Islam, they realized that this had been Satan.

Al-Hasan said concerning His words: ﴿And he said, "I am innocent of you; I see what you do not see"﴾: He said: Iblis saw Jibril (peace be upon him) wearing a cloak, walking before the Prophet (ﷺ), with a bridle in his hand leading the horse, without having mounted it.

Qatadah said: Iblis used to say, "I see what you do not see," and he spoke truly. And he said, ﴿"I fear Allah"﴾, and he lied. By Allah, there was no fear of Allah in him; rather he knew that there was no strength or protection in them, so he led them into destruction and abandoned them. This is the habit of the enemy of Allah toward those who obey him: when truth and falsehood meet, he abandons them and disowns them.

Ata' said: "I fear Allah" means: I fear that Allah will destroy me along with those who are destroyed.

Al-Kalbi said: He feared that Jibril (peace be upon him) would seize him and recognize his condition, and then they would not obey him.

It was also said: its meaning is, "I fear Allah," that is, "I know the truth of His promise to His friends, for he was certain of his affair."

﴿And Allah is severe in punishment﴾. It was also said: its meaning is, "I fear Allah for your sake, and Allah is severe in punishment." And it was said: the speech ends at His words "I fear Allah," and then Allah says: "And Allah is severe in punishment."

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Ibrahim ibn Abi 'Ulayyah, from Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Kurayz, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Satan was never seen on any day smaller, more humiliated, more despised, or more enraged than on the Day of 'Arafah, and that is only because of what he sees of the descent of mercy and Allah's forgiveness of great sins, except what happened on the Day of Badr." It was asked: "And what did he see on the Day of Badr?" He said: "Indeed he saw Jibril (peace be upon him) marshalling the angels." This is a mursal hadith. [[Narrated as a mursal by Imam Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Hajj, Bab Jami' al-Hajj: 1/422; and by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 5/17–18; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/158.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 49–50:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease say﴾ "Disease" means doubt and hypocrisy. ﴿Their religion has deluded these﴾, meaning: their religion has deluded the believers. These were a people who were oppressed in Makkah, who had embraced Islam, but whose relatives held them back from emigrating (hijrah). When the Quraysh set out for Badr, they took them out by force. When they saw the small number of the Muslims, they doubted and apostatised, and they said: "Their religion has deluded these." So they were all killed. Among them were: Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and Abu Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughirah, both of the Makhzum clan; al-Harith ibn Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib; Ali ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi; and al-As ibn Munabbih ibn al-Hajjaj. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah﴾, that is: whoever entrusts his affair to Allah and trusts in Him, ﴿then indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might﴾, strong, who does to His enemies whatever He wills, ﴿Wise﴾.

﴿And if you could see﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿when the angels take those who disbelieve, striking﴾, that is: taking their souls. Scholars differ regarding this. It has been said: this refers to the moment of death, when the angels strike the faces and backs of the disbelievers with whips of fire.

It has also been said: it refers to the polytheists who were killed at Badr, when the angels were striking ﴿their faces and their backs﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: it means their buttocks, but Allah is Modest and uses euphemism. Ibn Abbas said: when the polytheists advanced with their faces toward the Muslims, the angels struck their faces with swords; and when they turned back, the angels overtook them and struck their backs.

Ibn Jurayj said: it means what came before them and what went behind them, that is, they struck their entire bodies. The "taking" (tawaffi) here means killing.

﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾, that is: the angels will say to them: "Taste the punishment of the burning." It has also been said: the angels had iron maces with which they struck the disbelievers, and the fire would blaze in their wounds; this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And taste the punishment of the burning﴾. Al-Hasan said: this is the Day of Resurrection, when the keepers of Hell will say to them: "Taste the punishment of the burning." Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: they say this to them after death.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 59–60:

The words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that they have escaped﴾. Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah and Hafs read "yahsabanna" with the letter ya', while the others read it with the letter ta'. "Sabaqu" means "they came" (fa-ataw). It was revealed concerning those among the polytheists who fled on the Day of Badr. Whoever reads with ya' means: "let not those who disbelieve" think of themselves as having escaped and outrun Our punishment. Whoever reads with ta' is addressing (the believers) directly. Ibn 'Amir read ﴿that they cannot escape﴾ with a fathah on the alif, meaning: "because they cannot escape, and they will not get away from Me." The others read it with a kasrah on the alif, as a fresh beginning (ibtida', an independent sentence).

The words of Allah Most High: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power﴾. I'dad (preparation) means acquiring a thing for the time of need.

﴿Of power﴾, i.e., of the implements that give you power over them, such as horses and weapons.

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us, from Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj: Harun ibn Ma'ruf related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu 'Ali, Thumamah ibn Shufay, that he heard 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say while he was on the pulpit: "And prepare against them whatever you can of power. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery." [Narrated by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of archery, no. (1917): 3/1522.]

With this same chain he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Romans will be conquered for you, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will suffice you, so let none of you be unable to amuse himself with his arrows." [Narrated by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of archery, no. (1917): 3/1522.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aimi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Abu Nu'aym related to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil related to us, from Hamzah ibn Abi Usayd, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of Badr, when we had lined up against Quraysh and they had lined up against us: "When they come close to you, then use the arrows." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on urging archery: 6/91, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/61.]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani related to us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh related to us: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith related to us: Hisham al-Dastuwa'i related to us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu Najih al-Sulami, who said: We besieged al-Ta'if with the Prophet (ﷺ), and I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever reaches (the target) with an arrow in the way of Allah, it is for him a degree in Paradise." He said: On that day I reached sixteen arrows. And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever shoots an arrow in the way of Allah, it is equal to freeing a slave." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-'Itq, chapter on which slaves are best: 5/425; al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Jihad, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of archery: 5/267-268, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; al-Nasa'i in al-Jihad, chapter on the virtue of one who shoots an arrow: 6/27; al-Hakim: 2/121, and he said: this is a sahih hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, and al-Dhahabi agreed; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/386; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/383.]

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu al-Husayn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bishran informed us: Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi related to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Yahya ibn Kathir, from Zayd ibn Sallam, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn al-Azraq, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, Allah admits three people into Paradise through a single arrow: the one who makes it, the one who supplies it, and the one who shoots it in the way of Allah." [Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, no. (19522), and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/154. 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Azraq was declared trustworthy only by Ibn Hibban, and Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him without citing any criticism or praise of him.]

It is also related from Khalid ibn Zayd, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, Allah admits three persons into Paradise through a single arrow: its maker, who seeks reward through his craft for good; the one who shoots with it and the one who supplies it. Shoot and ride, but that you shoot is more beloved to me than that you ride. Every pastime a man engages in is vain, except his shooting with his bow, his training of his horse, and his playing with his wife, for these are of the truth. Whoever abandons archery after having learned it, out of distaste for it, has abandoned a blessing, or he said: has disbelieved in it." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on archery: 3/370; al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Jihad, chapter on the virtue of archery: 5/265-266, and he said: this is a hasan hadith (without his saying: "whoever abandons archery"); al-Nasa'i in al-Khayl, chapter on a man training his horse: 6/222-223; Ibn Majah in al-Jihad, chapter on archery in the way of Allah (2811): 2/940 with the wording of al-Tirmidhi; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/95 and al-Dhahabi agreed; and Imam Ahmad: 4/144.]

The words: ﴿And from steeds of war﴾, meaning: tethering them and keeping them for raiding. 'Ikrimah said: "power" refers to fortresses, and "steeds of war" refers to females. It is related from Khalid ibn al-Walid that he would not ride in battle except females, because of their low neighing. And from Abu Muhayriz, who said: The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, preferred male horses at the lines of battle and female horses for night raids and sudden attacks.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aimi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Abu Nu'aym related to us: Zakariyya related to us, from 'Amir: 'Urwah al-Bariqi related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Horses have goodness tied to their foreheads until the Day of Resurrection: reward and spoils." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on jihad continuing with the righteous and the wicked: 6/56; Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on goodness being in the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection (1872): 3/1493; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/385.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aimi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: 'Ali ibn Hafs related to us: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us: Talhah ibn Abi Sa'id related to us, saying: I heard Sa'id al-Maqburi narrate that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever keeps a horse in the way of Allah, out of faith and belief in His promise, then its eating, its drinking, its dung and its urine are in his scale on the Day of Resurrection." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on one who keeps a horse: 6/57, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/388.]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Horses are of three kinds: for one man it is a reward, for another a covering, and for another a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward: a man who tethers it in the way of Allah and lengthens its tether in a meadow or garden, so whatever it eats from that meadow or garden is recorded as good deeds for him; and if it breaks its tether and runs a stretch or two, its tracks and dung are good deeds for him; and if it passes by a river and drinks from it, though he did not intend to water it, that too is recorded for him as good deeds. So for that man it is a reward. As for the one for whom it is a covering: a man who tethers it out of self-sufficiency and chastity, and does not forget Allah's right in its backs or its necks, so it is a covering for him. As for the one for whom it is a burden: a man who tethers it out of pride, showing off, and enmity toward the people of Islam, so it is a burden upon him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about donkeys, and he said: "Nothing has been revealed to me concerning them except this comprehensive, unique verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on horses for three...: 6/63-64, and in the chapters on drinking, the prophets, tafsir and i'tisam; Muslim in al-Zakah with a longer version, chapter on the sin of withholding zakah (987): 2/680-682; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/24.]

﴿You will strike terror thereby﴾: you will frighten ﴿the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others﴾, i.e., and you will strike terror into others ﴿besides them, whom you do not know; Allah knows them﴾. Mujahid, Muqatil and Qatadah said: they are the Banu Qurayzah. al-Suddi said: they are the people of Persia. al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: they are the hypocrites, whom you do not know, because they are with you saying: "There is no god but Allah." It was also said: they are the disbelieving jinn.

﴿And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be repaid to you﴾: its reward will be paid to you in full, ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾: your rewards will not be diminished.

Ibn 'Amir read ﴿that they cannot escape﴾ with a fathah on the alif, meaning: "because they cannot escape, and they will not get away from Me." The others read it with a kasrah on the alif, as a fresh beginning (ibtida', an independent sentence).

The words of Allah Most High: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of power﴾. I'dad (preparation) means acquiring a thing for the time of need.

﴿Of power﴾, i.e., of the implements that give you power over them, such as horses and weapons.

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us, from Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj: Harun ibn Ma'ruf related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Abu 'Ali, Thumamah ibn Shufay, that he heard 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say while he was on the pulpit: "And prepare against them whatever you can of power. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery." [Narrated by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of archery, no. (1917): 3/1522.]

With this same chain he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Romans will be conquered for you, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will suffice you, so let none of you be unable to amuse himself with his arrows." [Narrated by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of archery, no. (1917): 3/1522.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aimi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Abu Nu'aym related to us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Ghasil related to us, from Hamzah ibn Abi Usayd, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of Badr, when we had lined up against Quraysh and they had lined up against us: "When they come close to you, then use the arrows." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on urging archery: 6/91, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/61.]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani related to us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh related to us: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith related to us: Hisham al-Dastuwa'i related to us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu Najih al-Sulami, who said: We besieged al-Ta'if with the Prophet (ﷺ), and I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever reaches (the target) with an arrow in the way of Allah, it is for him a degree in Paradise." He said: On that day I reached sixteen arrows. And I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever shoots an arrow in the way of Allah, it is equal to freeing a slave." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-'Itq, chapter on which slaves are best: 5/425; al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Jihad, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of archery: 5/267-268, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; al-Nasa'i in al-Jihad, chapter on the virtue of one who shoots an arrow: 6/27; al-Hakim: 2/121, and he said: this is a sahih hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, and al-Dhahabi agreed; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/386; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/383.]

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu al-Husayn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bishran informed us: Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi related to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us: Ma'mar informed us, from Yahya ibn Kathir, from Zayd ibn Sallam, from 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn al-Azraq, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, Allah admits three people into Paradise through a single arrow: the one who makes it, the one who supplies it, and the one who shoots it in the way of Allah." [Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, no. (19522), and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/154. 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd al-Azraq was declared trustworthy only by Ibn Hibban, and Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him without citing any criticism or praise of him.]

It is also related from Khalid ibn Zayd, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, Allah admits three persons into Paradise through a single arrow: its maker, who seeks reward through his craft for good; the one who shoots with it and the one who supplies it. Shoot and ride, but that you shoot is more beloved to me than that you ride. Every pastime a man engages in is vain, except his shooting with his bow, his training of his horse, and his playing with his wife, for these are of the truth. Whoever abandons archery after having learned it, out of distaste for it, has abandoned a blessing, or he said: has disbelieved in it." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on archery: 3/370; al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Jihad, chapter on the virtue of archery: 5/265-266, and he said: this is a hasan hadith (without his saying: "whoever abandons archery"); al-Nasa'i in al-Khayl, chapter on a man training his horse: 6/222-223; Ibn Majah in al-Jihad, chapter on archery in the way of Allah (2811): 2/940 with the wording of al-Tirmidhi; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/95 and al-Dhahabi agreed; and Imam Ahmad: 4/144.]

The words: ﴿And from steeds of war﴾, meaning: tethering them and keeping them for raiding. 'Ikrimah said: "power" refers to fortresses, and "steeds of war" refers to females. It is related from Khalid ibn al-Walid that he would not ride in battle except females, because of their low neighing. And from Abu Muhayriz, who said: The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, preferred male horses at the lines of battle and female horses for night raids and sudden attacks.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aimi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Abu Nu'aym related to us: Zakariyya related to us, from 'Amir: 'Urwah al-Bariqi related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Horses have goodness tied to their foreheads until the Day of Resurrection: reward and spoils." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on jihad continuing with the righteous and the wicked: 6/56; Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on goodness being in the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection (1872): 3/1493; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/385.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliki informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aimi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: 'Ali ibn Hafs related to us: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us: Talhah ibn Abi Sa'id related to us, saying: I heard Sa'id al-Maqburi narrate that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever keeps a horse in the way of Allah, out of faith and belief in His promise, then its eating, its drinking, its dung and its urine are in his scale on the Day of Resurrection." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on one who keeps a horse: 6/57, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/388.]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Horses are of three kinds: for one man it is a reward, for another a covering, and for another a burden. As for the one for whom it is a reward: a man who tethers it in the way of Allah and lengthens its tether in a meadow or garden, so whatever it eats from that meadow or garden is recorded as good deeds for him; and if it breaks its tether and runs a stretch or two, its tracks and dung are good deeds for him; and if it passes by a river and drinks from it, though he did not intend to water it, that too is recorded for him as good deeds. So for that man it is a reward. As for the one for whom it is a covering: a man who tethers it out of self-sufficiency and chastity, and does not forget Allah's right in its backs or its necks, so it is a covering for him. As for the one for whom it is a burden: a man who tethers it out of pride, showing off, and enmity toward the people of Islam, so it is a burden upon him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about donkeys, and he said: "Nothing has been revealed to me concerning them except this comprehensive, unique verse: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on horses for three...: 6/63-64, and in the chapters on drinking, the prophets, tafsir and i'tisam; Muslim in al-Zakah with a longer version, chapter on the sin of withholding zakah (987): 2/680-682; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/24.]

﴿You will strike terror thereby﴾: you will frighten ﴿the enemy of Allah and your enemy, and others﴾, i.e., and you will strike terror into others ﴿besides them, whom you do not know; Allah knows them﴾. Mujahid, Muqatil and Qatadah said: they are the Banu Qurayzah. al-Suddi said: they are the people of Persia. al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: they are the hypocrites, whom you do not know, because they are with you saying: "There is no god but Allah." It was also said: they are the disbelieving jinn.

﴿And whatever you spend in the way of Allah will be repaid to you﴾: its reward will be paid to you in full, ﴿and you will not be wronged﴾: your rewards will not be diminished.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verses 61–64:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾, meaning: if they incline toward reconciliation, ﴿then incline to it﴾, meaning: turn toward it and make peace with them. It is narrated from Qatadah and al-Hasan that this verse was abrogated (mansukhah, i.e. superseded by a later ruling, *naskh*) by His saying: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ (Bara'ah 5) [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, 10/34 (Halabi edition), and then he said of it: "It is a view for which there is no evidence from the Book, nor the Sunnah, nor the sound intellect's innate nature. We have shown in more than one place in this our book, the Tafsir, and elsewhere, that an abrogating ruling can only be that which negates the abrogated ruling in every respect. As for what is otherwise, it is not an abrogation. God's saying in Bara'ah, ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, does not negate the ruling of His saying, ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it﴾, because His saying ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾ refers only to the Banu Qurayzah, who were Jews, People of the Book. God, may His praise be exalted, permitted the believers to make peace with the People of the Book and to cease fighting them in exchange for taking the jizyah (poll tax) from them. As for His saying ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾, it refers only to the polytheist Arabs, the idol-worshippers, from whom the jizyah may not be accepted. So neither of the two verses negates the ruling of the other; rather, each of them is muhkam (firm, operative) regarding what it was revealed for."]]. ﴿And put your trust in God﴾, meaning: rely upon God and not upon others. ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.

﴿And if they intend to deceive you﴾, meaning: to betray you and plot against you. Mujahid said: it refers to the Banu Qurayzah.

﴿Then indeed, God is sufficient for you﴾, meaning: God is your sufficiency. ﴿It is He who supported you with His help and with the believers﴾, meaning: with the Ansar.

﴿And He brought their hearts together﴾, meaning: between the Aws and the Khazraj. There had been enmities and blood feuds between them in the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam), and God made them brothers after they had been enemies. ﴿Had you spent all that is on earth, you could not have brought their hearts together, but God brought them together. Indeed, He is Almighty, All-Wise.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, God is sufficient for you and for those believers who follow you.﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Thirty-three men and six women embraced Islam with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), then Umar ibn al-Khattab embraced Islam and the number was completed to forty, and then this verse was revealed [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 273.]].

The scholars differed concerning the grammatical position (*mahall*) of *man* (in ﴿and those who follow you﴾). Most of the exegetes said its position is in the genitive (khafd), being conjoined (*'atf*) to the *kaf* (the pronoun "you") in His saying "God is sufficient for you", so the meaning is: God is sufficient for you and for those who follow you. Others said it is in the nominative (raf'), being conjoined to the name "God", so the meaning is: God is sufficient for you, and so are your followers among the believers.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, urge the believers to fight﴾, meaning: urge them on to fight.

﴿If there are twenty among you﴾ men ﴿who are steadfast﴾, seeking reward, ﴿they will overcome two hundred﴾ of their enemy, subduing them. ﴿And if there are a hundred among you﴾ who are steadfast and seeking reward, ﴿they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve﴾. That is ﴿because they are a people who do not understand﴾. Meaning: the polytheists fight without seeking reward or pursuing a recompense, and they do not stand firm when you engage them in battle, out of fear of being killed. This is a report that carries the meaning of a command. This was the day of Badr. God obligated each believing man to fight ten disbelievers. This weighed heavily on the believers, so God lightened it for them, and then this was revealed:

﴿Now God has lightened your burden, for He knows that there is weakness in you﴾, meaning: weakness in the individual against fighting ten, and in the hundred against fighting a thousand. Abu Ja'far recited "ḍu'afā'" (weak ones), with a fatḥah on the ʿayn and a long vowel, as a plural. The others recited it with a sukūn on the ʿayn. ﴿So if there are a hundred steadfast among you, they will overcome two hundred﴾ of the disbelievers, ﴿and if there are a thousand among you, they will overcome two thousand, by God's permission. And God is with the steadfast﴾. Thus the ratio was reduced from ten to two. If the Muslims are at half the strength of their enemy, it is not permissible for them to flee.

Sufyan said: Ibn Shubruma said: I consider enjoining good and forbidding evil to be like this.

The people of Kufa recited "wa-in yakun minkum mi'atun" with the yā' in both places (i.e., yakun and yakun), agreeing with the people of Basra in the first instance. The rest recited with the tā' in both places. ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza recited "ḍu'afā'" with a fatḥah on the ḍād here and in Surat al-Rum, while the rest recited it with a ḍammah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives﴾. Abu Ja'far and the people of Basra recited "takūna" with the tā', while the rest recited it with the yā'. Abu Ja'far recited "asārā", and the others recited "asrā".

Al-A'mash narrated from ʿUmar ibn Murra, from Abu ʿUbayd, from ʿAbdullah ibn Mas'ud (may God be pleased with him), who said: On the day of Badr the captives were brought in. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What do you say about these?" Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of God, they are your people and your family. Spare them and give them time, perhaps God will accept their repentance. Take ransom from them, which will be a strength for us against the disbelievers." ʿUmar (may God be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of God, they denied you and drove you out. Bring them forward and we will strike their necks. Let ʿAlī have ʿAqīl so he may strike his neck, and let me have so-and-so, a relative of ʿUmar, so I may strike his neck, for these are the leaders of disbelief." ʿAbdullah ibn Rawaha said: "O Messenger of God, look for a valley rich in firewood, put them into it, then set a fire upon them." Al-ʿAbbas said to him: "You have cut off your kinship ties." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) fell silent and did not answer them, then he went inside. Some people said: he will take the view of Abu Bakr; some said: he will take the view of ʿUmar; some said: he will take the view of Ibn Rawaha. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) came out and said: "God, exalted is He, softens the hearts of some men until they become softer than milk, and hardens the hearts of other men until they become harder than stones. **The Qur'an: "Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already gone before"**

Ibn 'Abbas said: The spoils of war were forbidden to the prophets and the earlier nations. Whenever they took any spoils, they would set them aside as an offering (*lil-qurban*) [[In "A" it reads "kana" (was).]], and a fire would descend from heaven and consume it. When the Battle of Badr came, the believers rushed to take the spoils and accepted ransom (*fida'*). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already gone before" [[Al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Mardawayh (al-Durr: 4/111).]], meaning: had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already gone before in the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*), that He would make the spoils lawful for you.

Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already gone before," meaning that He would not punish anyone who had witnessed Badr with the Prophet (ﷺ) [[See: al-Tabari: 10/47.]].

Ibn Juraij said: "Had it not been for a decree from Allah that had already gone before," meaning that He does not lead a people astray after He has guided them until He has made clear to them what they should guard against, and that He does not seize a people for things they did in ignorance [[See: al-Tabari: 10/47.]]. "Surely a great punishment would have touched you" ﴿لَمَسَّكُمْ﴾ (*lamassakum*: would have touched you) ﴿لنا لكم﴾ [meaning: lam and lakum] "for what you took" ﴿فِيمَا أَخَذْتُمْ﴾ of the ransom, "before you were commanded to do so" ﴿قَبْلَ أَنْ تُؤْمَرُوا بِهِ﴾, ﴿عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾.

Ibn Ishaq said: None of the believers who were present failed to love the spoils, except 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who advised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to kill the captives. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of Allah, inflicting heavy slaughter (*al-ithkhan fi al-qatl*) was dearer to me than sparing the men." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had a punishment descended from heaven, none would have escaped it except 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/71. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Kafi al-Shaf" p. (71): "al-Waqidi narrated it in his Maghazi from another, disconnected route, with the same meaning, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a hadith from Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet: 'Had the punishment descended, none would have escaped it except Ibn al-Khattab.'" See also: Abu 'Ubayd's al-Amwal pp. (136–137).]].

Then Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿So eat of what you have gained of war booty, lawful and good; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. It is narrated that when the first verse was revealed, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) withheld their hands from what they had taken of the ransom, and then this was revealed: ﴿So eat of what you have gained﴾, and so on. We have also narrated from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and they were not made lawful for anyone before me" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tayammum: 1/435–436, and in al-Masajid and al-Jihad; and by Muslim in al-Masajid wa Mawadi' al-Salat, no. (521): 1/370–371; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/196.]].

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in "al-Kafi al-Shaf" p. (71): "al-Waqidi narrated it in his Maghazi from another, disconnected route, with the same meaning, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated a hadith from Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet: 'Had the punishment descended, none would have escaped it except Ibn al-Khattab.'" See also: Abu 'Ubayd's al-Amwal pp. (136–137).]].

Then Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿So eat of what you have gained of war booty, lawful and good; and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. It is narrated that when the first verse was revealed, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) withheld their hands from what they had taken of the ransom, and then this was revealed: ﴿So eat of what you have gained﴾, and so on. We have also narrated from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Spoils of war have been made lawful for me, and they were not made lawful for anyone before me" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tayammum: 1/435–436, and in al-Masajid and al-Jihad; and by Muslim in al-Masajid wa Mawadi' al-Salat, no. (521): 1/370–371; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/196.]].

Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us: Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam, who narrated to us from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The spoils of war were not made lawful for anyone before us, because Allah saw our weakness and inability, so He made them good for us" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fard al-Khumus, chapter "The spoils were not made lawful for anyone before us...", 6/220, and by Muslim in full, and the wording is his, in al-Jihad, chapter "The Making Lawful of Spoils..." (1747): 3/1366–1367.]].

O Prophet, say to those prisoners who are in your hands: ﴿O Prophet, say to whoever is in your hands of the captives...﴾

Abu 'Amr and Abu Ja'far read "min al-asara" (مِنَ الْأَسَارَى) with an alif, while the rest read it without the alif.

It was revealed concerning al-Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him), who was taken captive on the Day of Badr. He was one of the ten who guaranteed the food of the people of Badr (ḍamina ṭa'am ahl Badr), and it was his turn on the day of Badr. He had come out with twenty uqiyyah of gold in order to feed the people with it, but the fighting broke out, and the twenty uqiyyah remained with him and were taken from him in the battle. He spoke to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking that the twenty uqiyyah be counted from his ransom, but he refused and said: "As for the wealth you came out with to use against us, I will not leave it to you." He was then obligated to pay the ransom for his two nephews, 'Aqil ibn Abi Talib and Nawfal ibn al-Harith. Al-Abbas said: "O Muhammad, will you leave me to beg from Quraysh for as long as I live?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then where is the gold that you gave to Umm al-Fadl when you left Makkah, and you said to her: 'I do not know what may befall me on this journey, so if something happens to me, it is yours and for 'Abd Allah, 'Ubayd Allah, al-Fadl and Qutham'?" — meaning, his son. Al-Abbas said to him: "How do you know that?" He said: "My Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, informed me of it." Al-Abbas said: "I bear witness that you are truthful, and that there is no god but Allah and that you are His servant and Messenger, for no one had knowledge of it except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." This is the meaning of His words: ﴿O Prophet, say to whoever is in your hands of the captives﴾, those from whom you took the ransom, ﴿If Allah knows any good in your hearts﴾, i.e., faith, ﴿He will give you better than what was taken from you﴾, of the ransom, ﴿and forgive you﴾

your sins. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [Al-Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said:] Then Allah replaced it for me with twenty slaves, every one of whom trades with abundant wealth, and the least of them invests twenty thousand dirhams in place of the twenty uqiyyah. He gave me Zamzam, and I would not wish to have in exchange for it all the wealth of the people of Makkah, and I am awaiting forgiveness from my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic. [Narrated by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul from al-Kalbi, p. 276; al-Tabari 14/73; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 3/324 from 'A'ishah, who said: "Sahih according to the conditions of Muslim, though they did not record it." al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7/28: "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat and al-Kabir in abridged form; the men of al-Awsat are the men of the Sahih except Ibn Ishaq, who explicitly stated hearing it, and part of it is in the Sahih." See also al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 71.]

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And if they intend to betray you﴾, meaning the captives, ﴿they had already betrayed Allah before, so He gave you power over them﴾ at Badr, ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ Ibn Jurayj said: He meant by treachery disbelief; i.e., if they disbelieve in you, they had already disbelieved in Allah before, so He enabled the believers over them at Badr until they killed them and took them captive. And this is a warning to them if they return to fighting the believers and opposing them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 72–74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and emigrated﴾ — i.e., they forsook their people and their homelands, meaning the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun).

﴿and strove with their wealth and their lives in the cause of Allah, and those who sheltered [the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)] and the Emigrants with him, i.e., they housed them in their dwellings, and gave aid﴾ — i.e., they gave them victory against their enemies; these are the Helpers (al-Ansar), may Allah be pleased with them. ﴿Those are allies of one another﴾, to the exclusion of their kin among the disbelievers. It was said: [this refers to] assistance and support. Ibn 'Abbas said: [it refers to] inheritance. They used to inherit from one another on account of emigration, so the Emigrants and the Helpers inherited from one another to the exclusion of blood relatives. Whoever believed but did not emigrate did not inherit from his emigrant relative, until the Conquest of Makkah came and emigration ceased, and they inherited through kinship wherever they were. This ruling was abrogated (mansukh) by His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: [[See: al-Tabari: 14/68, edited by Mahmud Shakir.]] "And blood relatives are closer to one another in the Book of Allah" (al-Ahzab: 6). ﴿As for those who believed but did not emigrate, you owe them no duty of protection (wilayah) until they emigrate﴾ — i.e., inheritance. Hamza read "wa-la yatihim" with a kasra on the waw, while the rest read it with a fatha; both are the same, like al-dilalah and al-dalalah.

﴿And if they seek your help in religion﴾ — i.e., the believers who did not emigrate seek your help, ﴿then it is incumbent upon you to help, except against a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾ — a pact; so do not help them against them. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieve are allies of one another﴾ — in assistance and support. Ibn 'Abbas said: [it refers to] inheritance, i.e., the polytheists inherit from one another. ﴿Unless you do it, there will be discord in the land﴾ — Ibn 'Abbas said: unless you act upon the inheritance ruling which I have commanded you.

Ibn Jurayj said: unless you cooperate and support one another.

Ibn Ishaq said: Allah made the Emigrants and the Helpers a community of wilayah in religion, to the exclusion of others, and made the disbelievers allies of one another. Then He said: ﴿Unless you do it﴾, which is that a believer should take a disbeliever as an ally rather than a believer, ﴿there will be discord in the land and great corruption﴾. So "discord in the land" is the strengthening of disbelief, and "great corruption" is the weakening of Islam.

﴿Those who believed and emigrated and strove in the cause of Allah, and those who sheltered and helped — those are the believers truly﴾ — there is no doubt or uncertainty concerning their faith. It was said: they realized their faith through emigration, jihad, and spending wealth in the religion. ﴿For them is forgiveness and generous provision﴾ — in Paradise. If it is asked: what is the purpose of repeating this verse? It is said: the Emigrants were of several grades. Some of them were the people of the First Emigration, who emigrated before al-Hudaybiyah; some were the people of the Second Emigration, who emigrated after the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah and before the Conquest of Makkah; and some were doubly emigrants, [having made both] the emigration to Abyssinia and the emigration to Madinah. Thus the first verse refers to the First Emigration, and the second to the Second Emigration.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 8, verse 75:

His saying: ﴿And those who believed afterward and emigrated and strove alongside you — they are of you﴾, meaning: alongside you. He intends: you are of them, and he is of you. ﴿But relatives are more entitled to one another﴾. This abrogated inheritance by virtue of emigration and returned the inheritance to the kinsmen (dhawu al-arham).

His saying ﴿in the Book of Allah﴾, meaning: in the judgment of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It was also said: by the Book of Allah He meant the Qur'an, that is, the division which He explained in Surat al-Nisa'. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things﴾.

Surat al-Tawbah

Muqatil said: this surah is Medinan except for the last two verses of the surah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: Surat al-Tawbah? He said: It is al-Fadihah (the Disgracer); it kept descending, "And among them...", "And among them...", until they thought it would not leave any one of them without being mentioned in it. He said: I said, Surat al-Anfal? He said: That is the surah of Badr. He said: I said, Surat al-Hashr? He said: Say, the surah of Banu al-Nadir. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (4/120) to Abu 'Ubayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh, abridged.]]

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us, Abu al-Husayn 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Jurjani informed us, Abu Ahmad 'Abd Allah ibn 'Adi al-Hafiz informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Muthanna informed us, 'Ubayd Allah al-Qawariri narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, 'Awf ibn Abi Jamilah al-A'rabi narrated to us, Yazid al-Farisi narrated to me, Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) narrated to me, saying: I said to 'Uthman ibn 'Affan (may Allah be pleased with him): What prompted you to proceed to al-Anfal, which is among the mathani, and to Bara'ah, which is among the mi'in, and you joined them together and did not write "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" between them, and placed them among the al-sab' al-tiwal?

'Uthman said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was one upon whom time would pass, and surahs of many verses would descend upon him. When something was revealed to him, he would call some of those who wrote for him and say: Place this verse in the surah in which such-and-such is mentioned. Al-Anfal was among what was revealed at Medina, and Bara'ah was among the last of what was revealed, and its story resembled its story, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away without explaining to us that it was from it. So for this reason I joined them together and did not write between them the line "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful", and I placed them among the al-sab' al-tiwal. [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Salah, chapter on whoever pronounced it aloud (bismillah al-rahman al-rahim): 1/380; and al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir: 8/477-480, who said: this is a hasan hadith (in another copy: hasan sahih), which we only know from the hadith of 'Awf from Yazid al-Farisi from Ibn 'Abbas, and Yazid al-Farisi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas more than one hadith, and it is said he is Yazid ibn Hurmuz. Also narrated by Ibn Hibban, p. 125 of Mawarid al-Zam'an, and al-Hakim: 2/221, 330, who said: its isnad is sahih though they did not record it, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. And Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/57, 69. Ibn Kathir attributed it to al-Nasa'i (Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/588), and al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar narrated it in Muwafaqat al-Khabr al-Khabr pp. 68-69 with its isnad to Abu Dawud and graded it hasan, and said: its narrators are the narrators of the sahih except Yazid al-Farisi. Ahmad Shakir weakened this hadith in his commentary on the Musnad: 1/329, and said: it is a weak hadith, rather a hadith without basis, all of whose narrations revolve around Yazid al-Farisi, who narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Awf ibn Abi Jamilah al-A'rabi alone narrated it from him, and he is trustworthy. Before him, Ibn 'Atiyyah weakened it, saying: this view is weakened by reasoning that the Book of Allah should be disputed in this manner. See: al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 6/398. See also: Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/332, 4/106, 588; Fada'il al-Qur'an (appended to the Tafsir) of Ibn Kathir, pp. 17-18; Sharh al-Sunnah of al-Baghawi: 4/518; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/119; Fath al-Qadir of al-Shawkani: 2/331-332.]]
